Debt Verification : A breakdown of the debt amount, including principal, interest, fees, and other charges as required under 12 CFR 1006.34 ( c ). I request confirmation that no negative information will be furnished to the credit bureaus during the validation process, per Regulation F guidance. Notification to Future Collectors : If you transfer or sell this account to another agency, they must also be informed of my dispute per 12 CFR 1006.30 ( d ) ( 1 ). Next Steps Please provide a written response to this request within the legally required timeframe. If you can not validate this debt, I expect you to promptly remove it from my credit report and cease all collection efforts.Additionally, I do not consent to any form of contact via email, phone, or text message. narrative: On XX/XX/scrub>, 2026, a business-related inbound Real-Time Payment ( XXXX ) push-to-card transaction in the amount of {$540.00} was executed through an external payment platform. Due to a routing error, these corporate funds were misrouted and deposited into an unrelated consumer retail account held at SoFi Bank, N.A. ( XXXX XXXX : XXXX ). Over the subsequent XXXX days, extensive efforts were made to recover this capital. SoFis XXXX XXXX XXXX explicitly admitted in writing under SoFi Case XXXX XXXXXXXX that they are in possession of these funds, that the money was deposited into the wrong account in error, and that their account holder has no legal claim to it. However, SoFi has actively obstructed the recovery process, claiming " there is nothing SoFi can do '' to return the money unless the originating merchant platform initiates a formal network pullback. When the originating platform attempted to coordinate, they required standard documentation from SoFi. Despite multiple requests, SoFi has failed to promptly issue a standardized administrative summary of their written findings on official bank letterhead to satisfy clearinghouse documentation needs, effectively insulating themselves and allowing their retail account holder to benefit from unjust enrichment. A financial institution can not knowingly hold and block the return of verified, misrouted corporate assets once a clear network audit trail and explicit admission of error have been established.

Case law, including XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), clarifies that while verification may be limited, it still requires confirmation that the debt is accurate and attributable to the consumer. The response provided does not sufficiently demonstrate that the alleged debt has been properly verified or substantiated beyond internal account records. Therefore, I dispute the adequacy of the validation provided and request proper documentation establishing the validity, accuracy, and legal right to collect.

narrative: URGENT CFPB COMPLAINT ACCOUNT CLOSED DUE TO ALLY BANK SYSTEM FAILURE I am filing an urgent complaint against Ally Bank regarding the wrongful closure of all my accounts following a documented system failure that prevented me from transferring funds between my own accounts. Summary of Issue My checking account became overdrawn. However, I had sufficient funds in another Ally Bank account to immediately resolve the overdraft. I attempted to transfer the funds, but Ally Bank was experiencing confirmed system outages that prevented transfers from being completed. During multiple calls with Ally representatives, including a supervisor, I was explicitly informed and they acknowledged that Ally was experiencing system issues. I have a recorded phone call documenting these admissions and can provide it upon request. Bank Failure and Account Closure Because Allys system failure prevented me from transferring my own funds, the overdraft remained unresolved. After approximately 30 days, Ally Bank closed ALL of my accounts instead of working with me to resolve a problem that was directly caused by its own system outage. This action is unfair and unreasonable because : * Funds were available within Ally Bank to cure the overdraft * I was actively attempting to resolve the issue * Ally Banks own system failure prevented completion of the transfer * Ally representatives acknowledged the system issues Financial Harm and Immediate Hardship Ally Bank informed me that it will take 710 days to return my remaining funds. In addition, I have an incoming payroll direct deposit through XXXX that Ally has stated will be rejected and returned to my employer due to the account closure. This will result in : * Immediate loss of access to my wages * At least a XXXX week delay in receiving my paycheck * XXXX financial hardship due to inability to access my own funds Evidence Available I have : * Recorded call with Ally representatives and a supervisor acknowledging system outages * Proof of available funds in another Ally account * Account records and closure notices * Payroll deposit information showing imminent wage disruption Requested Resolution I am requesting immediate CFPB intervention requiring Ally Bank to : 1. Review the account closure decision in light of documented system failures 2. Review recorded calls acknowledging the system outage 3. Expedite release of all remaining funds ( same-day or next-day ACH if possible ) 4. Reverse or correct the account closure status where appropriate 5. Prevent or mitigate disruption to incoming payroll funds 6. Remove any negative reporting resulting from this incident 7. Provide a written explanation of why internal system failure did not prevent account closure actions Closing Statement This situation was not caused by insufficient funds or customer negligence. It was caused by Ally Banks system failure preventing me from accessing and transferring my own money. I made reasonable and timely attempts to resolve the issue. I am now facing avoidable financial hardship, including loss of access to wages, as a direct result of this failure.

I. IMMEDIATE CEASE AND DESIST ON REPOSSESSION
Effective upon receipt of this letter, Ford Motor Credit Company LLC ("Ford") is directed to IMMEDIATELY CEASE AND DESIST all repossession activity, all instructions to recovery agents or third-party vendors, all vehicle-locating or surveillance activity, all repossession-related fees, and all further adverse credit reporting concerning the above-referenced account.

Any repossession action by Ford or any party acting on Ford's behalf taken in violation of this cease and desist will be treated as a final and dispositive act foreclosing all settlement discussion and will trigger a full damages claim under the statutes identified in Section III, including the fee-shifting provisions that make Ford liable for prevailing-consumer attorney fees.
A consumer-law attorney is currently reviewing the full evidentiary record of this account.
II. THE DOCUMENTED RECORD OF MY EFFORTS AND FORD'S NON-RESPONSE
This letter is not the start of a conversation. It is the documented final record of a conversation Ford has refused to have with me for the past nine months. I have been the only party actively attempting to resolve this account. The record shows the following:

I was actively retrieving statements newest-to-oldest, one at a time, when Ford disabled my online access mid-download. Ford's lockout screen states verbatim: "Because of your account status, we have disabled your online access." I retain timestamped XXXX screenshots of the lockout screen.

Previously raised in all prior submissions. This loan is documented as a simple-interest retail installment contract at 5.69% APR. On a simple-interest loan, daily interest equals (principal balance annual rate XXXX or XXXX). I am submitting this complaint regarding GRT Financial and requesting a review of its fee collection practices, account administration, and responses to my requests for information. I enrolled in a debt settlement program with GRT Financial that was projected to extend until approximately XX/XX/XXXX based on the payment schedule provided by GRT Financial. Four accounts were originally enrolled in the program : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I made my first payment into the program on XX/XX/XXXX. My regular program payment was {$440.00} semi-monthly ( approximately {$890.00} per month ), and I continued making those payments throughout the program except for one modified payment arrangement in XX/XX/XXXX that was made with GRT Financials agreement. According to GRT Financials records, two accounts were settled : XXXX XXXX ( original enrolled balance : {$23000.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX ( original enrolled balance : {$10000.00} ) The total original enrolled balance of these two settled accounts was {$34000.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a written summary from a GRT Financial supervisor providing a breakdown of fees collected, creditor payments made, and other program activity. The financial figures referenced in this complaint are derived from that written summary and information contained in my client portal. GRT Financial provided a written summary stating that : Total amount paid into the program : {$8500.00} Settlement fees collected : {$4600.00} Total paid to creditors : {$2000.00} Remaining settlement fees claimed by GRT Financial : {$4900.00} GRT Financial later provided information indicating that settlement fees assessed on the two settled accounts totaled approximately {$9500.00}. Based on GRT Financials own records, {$4600.00} in settlement fees were collected in less than XXXX year while only {$2000.00} was paid to creditors during that same period. I am requesting a review of whether this fee collection structure complies with the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule ( TSR ) and any other applicable consumer protection laws and regulations. In addition, I requested written explanations regarding my account on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. In these communications, I requested : The mathematical calculation used to determine my current payment amount ; The effective date of any payment adjustment resulting from the removal of accounts from the program ; An explanation of why my payment amount remained approximately {$890.00} per month after two of the four enrolled accounts were removed from the program ; A detailed calculation showing how settlement fees were determined, calculated, and earned. Although GRT Financial subsequently provided additional account summaries, fee totals, payment schedules, and general explanations regarding my program, it did not provide the specific calculations and methodologies I requested. GRT Financial informed me that after two of the four enrolled accounts were removed from the program, my monthly payment would remain approximately {$840.00} per month after the removal of the XXXX XXXX fee and that my projected program completion date would be accelerated from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. I am seeking clarification regarding the contractual, mathematical, and regulatory basis for maintaining approximately the same monthly payment while accelerating the projected completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. I do not understand how the removal of two of the four enrolled accounts resulted in a reduction of the projected program duration of approximately 15 months while maintaining approximately the same monthly payment, and I have not been provided sufficient calculations to independently verify that determination. Furthermore, on XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a GRT Financial escalation specialist regarding these issues. During that conversation, I was informed for the first time that GRT Financial had accelerated my projected program completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. Prior to that conversation, I had not been notified that my projected program completion date had been materially changed. I did not receive a telephone call, email, written notice, contract amendment, or other documentation informing me of this change before it was implemented. I also was not provided with a detailed calculation or explanation supporting the basis for the change. In addition, although GRT Financial informed me that my projected completion date had been accelerated to approximately XX/XX/XXXX, my online client portal continues to display scheduled ACH drafts extending into XXXX. I have not received a written explanation reconciling these two representations. As a result, I remain unable to determine my actual projected program completion date or independently verify the accuracy of the information being provided regarding my account. As of the date of this complaint, I still have not received : A complete mathematical calculation showing how my current payment amount was determined ; The numerical calculation supporting the decision to maintain approximately the same monthly payment after the removal of two enrolled accounts ; The contractual basis for accelerating my projected program completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX ; The formula, percentages, and methodology used to calculate settlement fees ; The basis upon which settlement fees were deemed earned ; The calculation supporting GRT Financials claim that additional settlement fees remain due. I am particularly concerned that less than XXXX year after enrollment, GRT Financial had collected {$4600.00} in settlement fees while only {$2000.00} had been paid to creditors. Despite repeated written requests, I have been unable to obtain sufficient documentation to independently verify how these fees were calculated, earned, and collected or to determine whether the fee collection structure complies with applicable law. I am also concerned that one of my creditors ultimately filed a lawsuit while I was enrolled in the program and making regular payments into the program. Although I attempted to resolve that matter independently by sending settlement proposals to the creditors attorneys, I remain concerned about the relationship between the programs fee collection structure and the amount of money that was ultimately paid to creditors. As a result of that lawsuit, the court filing became publicly available through court records and was subsequently indexed by third-party websites and internet search engines. This has caused me significant professional concern and has negatively affected my reputation. I respectfully request that the CFPB consider this as part of its review when evaluating whether GRT Financials fee collection practices and administration of my account complied with applicable consumer protection laws and regulations. I respectfully request that GRT Financial provide : A complete written accounting of all fees assessed ; The calculations used to determine those fees ; The basis upon which those fees were deemed earned ; The calculations supporting my payment amount ; The contractual basis for maintaining approximately the same payment amount while accelerating the projected completion date of the program ; An explanation of how its fee collection practices comply with applicable federal consumer protection laws and regulations. If the CFPB determines that GRT Financial improperly assessed or collected fees or otherwise failed to comply with applicable consumer protection laws or regulations, I respectfully request that appropriate relief be considered, including reimbursement of any fees determined to have been improperly assessed or collected. Thank you for your review of this matter.

narrative: Issue : Misleading account practices, withheld funds, inability to access wages, and account closure issues. Complaint : I am filing a complaint against EarnIn because I believe the company has failed to clearly explain how my wages were being held and used, and I have been unable to access the full amount of my paycheck. My employer deposited approximately {$910.00} of my paycheck into my EarnIn account through direct deposit. However, despite that deposit, my available balance was only approximately {$650.00}. Roughly {$260.00} of my own earnings was unavailable to me. The app represented that I had an available " Boost '' of around {$250.00}, but this was misleading because it appeared to simply be my own wages being released back to me rather than new funds or a loan. From my perspective, EarnIn was restricting access to money that I had already earned and then presenting access to those withheld wages as a benefit. When I contacted customer support to close my account, I explained that I wanted to close it because the fees and the way my paycheck was handled did not make sense. I specifically informed them that : My paycheck had been split between EarnIn and my XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account. Approximately {$910.00} was deposited into EarnIn. Only about {$650.00} was actually available to me. Around {$260.00} of my paycheck appeared to be withheld. I did not want to continue using the EarnIn account and wanted my remaining paycheck released so I could use my own credit union. Instead of explaining why my wages were unavailable or returning my money, EarnIn informed me that before they would close my account, I had to use my own " secured funds '' to pay off my EarnIn Card balance. Customer support stated that the " secured funds '' were portions of my earnings that EarnIn had reserved from my direct deposit to cover card activity. They instructed me to use those withheld wages to pay the account balance before they would allow the account to be closed. This is what concerns me. The money being withheld was my paycheck. If I no longer wanted to use the EarnIn card or account, I do not understand why EarnIn could retain part of my wages and require me to use those same withheld wages before closing the account. I requested to speak with a supervisor because I did not believe this was being adequately explained. I believe EarnIn 's practices are confusing and potentially misleading because : Consumers may not clearly understand that portions of their paycheck can become unavailable as " secured funds. '' The available balance may not accurately reflect the amount of wages deposited. Features such as " Boost '' may create the impression that consumers are receiving additional funds when they may simply be gaining access to wages that were already withheld. Customers attempting to close their accounts may effectively be prevented from doing so until EarnIn applies their own deposited wages toward account balances.

narrative: Subject : XX/XX/XXXX Supplemental CFPB Complaint Against NewRez/Shellpoint Regarding Unfounded Escrow Increase, XXXX Confirmation , Manufactured Default, Payoff Obstruction, and Improper Liquidation/DIL Pressure To Whom It May Concern : I am submitting this supplemental complaint against NewRez LLC d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing concerning my VA-backed mortgage loan for XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, TN XXXX, Loan No. XXXX. This supplement concerns a new escrow development discovered on XX/XX/XXXX, involving NewRezs use of an XXXX homeowners insurance figure to create or justify an additional escrow burden. Today, XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX confirmed to us that NewRez/Shellpoint can not use the {$2800.00} XXXX insurance amount as a new or additional escrow charge because that annual premium has already been handled through the escrow/mortgagee billing process. XXXX confirmed that NewRezs use of that amount to create an additional escrow basis is unfounded. XXXX confirmation also undermines NewRez/Shellpoints prior escrow calculations that forced the loan into default. The XXXX documents support this. The Evidence of Insurance dated XX/XX/XXXX identifies the policy period as XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, lists the annual premium as {$2800.00}, states the payor type is Escrow, and lists NEWREZ LLC XXXX XXXX as the mortgagee. The amended XXXX declaration also states the {$2800.00} is the total 12-month policy premium and expressly says, This is not a request for payment. Mortgagee has been billed. XXXX update letter states that the policy was updated effective XX/XX/XXXX and that the premium increased by {$400.00} for the current policy period. This means NewRez/Shellpoint appears to have taken a real annual insurance premium, stripped it from context, and used it to manufacture or support a new escrow/payment justification. The {$2800.00} is not a monthly payment, not a new borrower payment demand, not a separate additional escrow item, and not a new unpaid obligation outside the existing escrow process. It is an annual homeowners insurance premium, escrow-paid, with the mortgagee already billed. NewRezs own portal has created conflicting escrow narratives. One NewRez escrow screen states that the shortage was caused because taxes and/or insurance has changed, yet the projection table showed XXXX at {$2700.00} for the last 12 months and {$2700.00} for the next 12 months, with a {$0.00} difference. It also showed XXXX XXXX taxes at {$2300.00} for the last 12 months and {$2300.00} for the next 12 months, also with a {$0.00} difference. That means NewRezs stated explanation, taxes and/or insurance changed, conflicts with its own projection table. NewRezs portal now shows a negative escrow balance and a current escrow payment of {$870.00}, while also using XXXX insurance information to justify or reinforce the escrow increase. But XXXX has confirmed that NewRez can not use the {$2800.00} annual premium as a separate additional escrow demand because it has already been paid/accounted for through escrow. NewRezs use of that figure appears to be double counting, misapplication, or manipulation. This is not an isolated escrow question. NewRezs escrow calculations caused a payment increase, created unaffordability, and contributed to the default condition NewRez then used to pressure liquidation, payment assistance, deed-in-lieu, and surrender options. We previously told NewRez we would not sign a deed-in-lieu that offered no meaningful protection, no relocation assistance, no deficiency protection, no credit correction, no VA entitlement protection, and no resolution of the disputed escrow/payment figures. NewRez nevertheless continued to pursue liquidation-related conduct while failing to provide a clean and reliable explanation of the escrow account. This is especially serious because this is a VA-backed mortgage loan, and the escrow manipulation has affected default status, sale pressure, payoff reliability, bankruptcy harm, and VA entitlement risk. The regulatory issue is that escrow analyses are supposed to be based on actual or reasonably anticipated escrow disbursements. Regulation X requires escrow account analysis and annual escrow statements, and the analysis must itemize estimated taxes, insurance premiums, and other charges reasonably anticipated to be paid from escrow. NewRez can not use an already-paid or already-accounted-for annual insurance premium to create a second escrow obligation. Regulation X also requires servicers to respond to notices of error by correcting the error or conducting a reasonable investigation and providing a written explanation, including the reasons no error occurred and the borrowers right to request documents relied upon. NewRez has failed to provide a reliable explanation for the escrow shortage, the current escrow payment, the XXXX figures used, the prior {$2700.00} XXXX figure, and the basis for the claimed default. NewRez has also failed to timely provide a reliable payoff statement despite the urgent sale context. Federal mortgage servicing rules require a payoff statement within a reasonable time and generally no later than seven business days after a written request, subject to limited exceptions such as bankruptcy or foreclosure, where the statement still must be provided within a reasonable time. I ask CFPB to require NewRez/Shellpoint to provide the following : XXXX. The complete escrow transaction history from XX/XX/XXXX through present. XXXX. The complete escrow analysis worksheets for every escrow analysis or reanalysis performed in XXXX, including XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and any later internal or portal recalculations. XXXX. The source document supporting NewRezs prior XXXX figure of {$2700.00}. XXXX. The source document and accounting basis for NewRezs use of the {$2800.00} XXXX annual premium. XXXX. Proof of whether the XXXX {$2800.00} premium was paid, when it was paid, from what account it was paid, and whether it was already accounted for in escrow. XXXX. A written explanation of why NewRezs portal stated taxes and/or insurance changed while the same projection table showed {$0.00} difference for both XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. A written explanation of how NewRez calculated the current escrow payment of {$870.00}. XXXX. Immediate correction of any escrow overstatement, duplicate insurance charge, or unsupported shortage. XXXX. Immediate correction of the default status if the default was caused or materially worsened by NewRezs unsupported escrow calculations. XXXX. A reliable payoff statement suitable for closing, with escrow balance, fees, charges, bankruptcy coding, DIL fee, suspense/unapplied funds, and all corporate advances fully itemized. XXXX. Written confirmation that NewRez will not use a disputed, unfounded, or double-counted escrow figure to pressure deed-in-lieu, foreclosure, liquidation, sale obstruction, negative credit reporting, or VA claim activity. XXXX. Written confirmation that NewRez has notified VA Loan Guaranty of the corrected escrow/payment status and that no VA claim , foreclosure, or liquidation recommendation will rely on the disputed escrow calculations. NewRez/Shellpoints anticipated defense may be that it is permitted to project future escrow disbursements. That does not answer the issue. The issue is that NewRez appears to have used an already escrow-paid or already-accounted-for XXXX annual premium as if it supported a new additional escrow burden. XXXX has confirmed that NewRez can not use the {$2800.00} figure in that manner. NewRezs own portal also contradicts itself by claiming changed taxes/insurance while showing no change in taxes or insurance. This appears to be a manufactured escrow crisis. NewRez created or relied on unsupported escrow math, increased the payment, pushed the loan into default, then used that default pressure to pursue liquidation/DIL options while failing to provide a clean payoff or accurate accounting. This conduct has caused severe harm, including forced financial distress, bankruptcy consequences, sale uncertainty, VA entitlement risk, and loss of confidence in the payoff and escrow records. XXXX has also confirmed they are willing to testify to NewRez manipulating escrow based on unsupported insurance numbers. I request that CFPB treat this as an urgent mortgage servicing, escrow, payoff, and loss-mitigation complaint requiring immediate correction and production of the underlying source documents. Respectfully, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

I am submitting this complaint because * * Educational Credit Management Corporation ( ECMC ) * * continues to report a derogatory collection account on my consumer credit reports that I believe is inaccurate, incomplete, and has not been properly verified as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I have exercised my rights under the FCRA by disputing the accuracy of this account and requesting that the consumer reporting agencies conduct a reasonable reinvestigation. Rather than receiving documentation establishing the accuracy of the account, I have received only generalized responses indicating that the account was " verified '' or continues to be reported as accurate. These responses do not explain what information was reviewed, what records were relied upon, or how ECMC substantiated the information being reported. A statement that an account has been verified, without supporting evidence, does not satisfy the requirements of federal law. The ECMC account is currently being reported as a * * collection account with a derogatory status * *, and its continued presence on my credit reports has caused substantial harm to my financial standing. A collection account significantly affects creditworthiness and may negatively influence decisions regarding loans, credit cards, housing, employment, and insurance. Because of the serious impact this reporting has on my financial life, I requested that ECMC and the consumer reporting agencies conduct a thorough investigation using original source documentation rather than relying on automated electronic verification systems. Under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681i * *, when a consumer disputes information appearing on a credit report, the consumer reporting agency is required to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is accurate. Likewise, under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) * *, consumer reporting agencies must maintain reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information they report. These statutory obligations require more than transmitting an electronic dispute to the furnisher and accepting an automated response. They require an investigation based upon competent documentary evidence that establishes the accuracy and completeness of the information being reported. To date, I have not received any documentation demonstrating that ECMC possesses sufficient evidence to support the continued reporting of this collection account. I requested copies of the original promissory note or other legally binding agreement, documentation identifying me as the obligor, complete account records, payment history, account statements, records establishing the balance claimed to be owed, documentation showing the date of first delinquency, and any documents supporting the transfer or assignment of the account to ECMC if applicable. I also requested copies of the records relied upon during the investigation and an explanation of the method of verification used. Despite these requests, no competent documentary evidence has been provided. If ECMC maintains that the account is accurate, then it should have no difficulty producing complete business records establishing its accuracy. These records should include the original signed agreement or promissory note, complete servicing history, payment ledger, records supporting the balance reported, documentation establishing the date of default, records demonstrating that the account was lawfully transferred or assigned to ECMC if it was acquired from another entity, and documentation demonstrating ECMC 's authority to report and collect the alleged debt. Without this documentation, I have no way to determine whether the information appearing on my credit reports is accurate, complete, or legally reportable. I am also concerned that the investigation conducted by the consumer reporting agencies may have relied exclusively upon automated verification systems instead of an independent review of the underlying records. Numerous courts have recognized that a reasonable investigation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act requires more than accepting the furnisher 's computerized response when a consumer specifically disputes the accuracy of an account. A meaningful reinvestigation requires examination of the original source documents and consideration of the evidence presented by the consumer. If ECMC merely confirmed the account through an automated process without reviewing the original records, then the investigation was not reasonable within the meaning of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. In addition, I requested disclosure of the method of verification used during the investigation. Specifically, I requested identification of the individual or department that conducted the investigation, the documents that were reviewed, the records relied upon, and the procedures used to determine that the account was accurately reported. Instead of receiving this information, I received only a conclusory statement that the account had been verified. Such a response does not provide sufficient transparency to determine whether the investigation complied with federal law. The continued reporting of this ECMC collection account has caused ongoing damage to my consumer credit profile. Credit reports play an essential role in determining a consumer 's access to credit, housing, employment opportunities, and favorable financial terms. Because of the significant consequences associated with derogatory reporting, Congress enacted the Fair Credit Reporting Act to ensure that only information that is accurate, complete, and verifiable appears on consumer credit reports. Allowing inaccurate or unsupported information to remain on a consumer report undermines these important protections. I am not requesting the removal of accurate information simply because it is unfavorable. Rather, I am requesting that ECMC comply with its legal obligations by substantiating the disputed information with competent documentary evidence. If ECMC possesses original business records demonstrating that every aspect of its reporting is accurate, then those records should be produced. If ECMC can not produce the original documentation necessary to verify the account, then the account should not continue to be reported as a collection account on my consumer credit reports. Furthermore, I request that ECMC explain how it calculated the balance being reported, identify whether any interest, fees, penalties, or other charges were added, and provide documentation supporting those calculations. If the reported balance can not be fully supported by contemporaneous business records, then the information being reported can not be considered accurate under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. I also request documentation establishing the legal authority for ECMC to report this account. If ECMC acquired servicing rights or ownership of the alleged obligation from another entity, I request copies of any assignment agreements, transfer documentation, servicing records, or other evidence establishing its legal authority to report the account. If ECMC is unable to establish its legal authority through competent evidence, then it should not continue reporting this account to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau require ECMC and the consumer reporting agencies to conduct a complete and lawful reinvestigation of this disputed account. I request that ECMC provide copies of the original promissory note or agreement, complete payment history, servicing records, account statements, documentation supporting the reported balance, records establishing the date of first delinquency, documentation establishing any assignment or transfer of the account, and every document relied upon during its investigation. I also request disclosure of the method of verification used and an explanation of how ECMC concluded that the account was accurately reported. If ECMC can not produce competent documentary evidence establishing that this collection account is accurate, complete, and legally verifiable, I request that it be permanently deleted from all of my consumer credit reports. I further request written confirmation of the investigation results, copies of all documents relied upon, and an updated copy of my consumer credit reports reflecting the deletion of any information that can not be verified in accordance with * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) and 1681i * *. My request is based solely on my right to have consumer reporting that is accurate, complete, and supported by competent evidence as required by federal law.

Subject : REQUEST FOR XXXX XXXX STATEMENTS FOLLOWING ACCOUNT RESTRICTION To Whom It May Concern, I am filing this formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., regarding the lack of financial transparency and the denial of records following the restriction of my business checking account, held under my XXXX XXXX. I have been a compliant and consistent business client with Chase for the past three ( 3 ) years, maintaining an unblemished banking history. Approximately 100 days ago, Chase placed a restrictive hold on my account. Since the restriction, my online banking access has been completely revoked. I have made multiple phone calls to Chase Customer Service to resolve this matter ; however, during every call, the representatives have systematically refused to give me any details about what happened. Furthermore, instead of providing an official balance statement, the representative explicitly stated over the phone that my money was completely lost and that no further information or documentation can be provided to me. A financial institution can not simply tell a commercial customer that their funds are completely lost without providing an official accounting ledger or a formal written explanation. Therefore, I respectfully request the CFPB to compel JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . to : 1-Provide Details and Final Statements : Furnish the complete, itemized business bank statements covering the last 120 days so I can properly account for what happened. 2-Deliver a Detailed Accounting Ledger : Deliver an official written summary of all debits, reversals, or adjustments processed during the restriction period to show exactly how and why my corporate funds were removed. 3-Send Official Records : Mail the official financial documents to the registered business address of my LLC or deliver them securely via email to my verified contact address. Thank you for your prompt intervention in securing my legal right to my business 's financial data. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

narrative: I have been a U.S. Bank customer for XXXX years ( since XXXX ) and currently maintain another active U.S. Bank credit card. I also recently financed and paid off an auto loan through U.S. Bank. My credit card account, which had been open since XXXX, was recently closed for inactivity. During the period leading up to the closure, my family and I were dealing with an international family emergency. U.S. Bank sent notices stating that the account " XXXX '' be closed for inactivity. They did not say " will be closed. '' Had I understood that closure was imminent or certain, I would have made a small transaction in the midst of our emergency to keep the account active. Instead, while dealing with the emergency, I interpreted the notices as warnings rather than a final deadline, and hoped for grace from US bank given the circumstances. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted U.S. Bank regarding the closure. During my first chat, I was advised that the account could not be reopened. I was not given the opportunity to ask my follow-up questions, as the agent said goodbye and unilaterally ended the chat. Later that same day, I initiated a second chat as I was cut off by the first agent. I explained the emergency circumstances and my desire to preserve a banking relationship that has existed for XXXX years since XXXX. I was asked to provide my contact information and was then advised that my request had been submitted to Supervisors/Managers and that I would be contacted within XXXX hours.... No contact was received within the promised timeframe. On XX/XX/XXXX, after receiving no follow-up within 9 days ( despite being told XXXX hours ), I contacted U.S. Bank again . During that interaction, I was informed that the prior supervisor callback request had not even been submitted despite my having previously been told that it had been. After expressing disappointment, a new escalation request was submitted, and I was provided confirmation number XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX 9 days XXXX received a call from U.S. Bank 's complaint department from XXXX. During that call, I explained that the combination of our international family emergency and US bank using the phrase " we XXXX close your account '' contributed to my inability to address the inactivity notices. We found many of the responses unhelpful : I was advised that even if U.S. Bank had not provided warning notices, they retained the right to close the account at any time for any reason. I was also advised that had this issue arisen a year earlier, " we would be having a different conversation and I could help you '' but no further explanation was provided regarding what options may have existed previously. The representative also stated that " this is just the way the world is going. '' These explanations were particularly unhelpful, as we do not have the opportunity to " have the emergency a year earlier. '' And saying " we would have helped you in the past but can't now '' was not responsive to our concern or our situation. We had also requested a stateXXXX required lien release document. We spoke to a US Bank representative over the phone. We requested a physical copy be mailed to us. We also separately requested an electronic copy be sent to our email ( as the previous physical copy never reached us, so we wanted an electronic backup ). We were told both of these would be sent, but we never received it. XXXX mentioned " I know exactly what you are referring to '' however he said he would not be able to assist with this failed follow through either. My complaint is not limited to the denial of reinstatement. My concern is also the inconsistent information and repeated failed follow-through during the escalation process. I was specifically advised on XX/XX/XXXX that a supervisor review had been submitted and that I would receive contact within XXXX hours. I later learned that the request had apparently never been entered into the system and only became aware of this after proactively following up myself. Throughout this process, I repeatedly explained that I wished to preserve a banking relationship that has existed for XXXX years ( since XXXX ), and that I intended to continue using U.S. Bank for future banking and lending needs. The handling of this matter has caused us to reconsider that relationship. Having to spend this much effort for a lien release as well as a reconsideration of account closure, on top of our stressful international family emergency, left a lot to be desired in terms of customer service, grace, and understanding.

I am filing this complaint regarding the servicing of my mortgage by First Citizens Bank. I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) investigate the banks inaccurate billing practices, failure to update my mailing address despite multiple requests, improper payment processing, and inaccurate credit reporting that has negatively impacted my credit history. My first concern involves my mailing address. For several months, my mortgage statements were mailed to an incorrect address. I contacted First Citizens on at least XXXX occasions requesting that my mailing address be corrected. Despite these requests, the issue was not resolved until I informed the bank that I intended to file a complaint with the CFPB. Because my statements were not being sent to my correct address, I was unaware of changes made to my monthly mortgage payment and was deprived of timely notice regarding my account. My second concern involves an unexplained curtailment charge that appeared on my mortgage account in XX/XX/2026. A curtailment is generally a voluntary principal payment made by the borrower. I never requested, authorized, or agreed to any voluntary principal curtailment. Nevertheless, a {$240.00} curtailment charge was added to my account, increasing my monthly payment. Prior to this change, my monthly mortgage payment for principal, interest, and escrow was consistently approximately {$2400.00}. After the curtailment was added, my required payment unexpectedly increased to approximately {$2700.00} without any explanation or supporting documentation. My statements also began reflecting an overdue payment balance without any explanation of how that amount was calculated. The primary issue is the inaccurate reporting of a XXXX late payment to the credit reporting agencies. On XX/XX/2026, I submitted a mortgage payment of {$2700.00} through First Citizens payment system. On XX/XX/2026, I submitted another payment of {$2700.00}. Even if the bank believed my XX/XX/XXXX payment was insufficient because of the unexplained payment increase, I made another substantial payment before a full billing cycle had elapsed. Based on the payments I made, I do not understand how my account could have legitimately become 30 days delinquent. I also discovered another concerning issue regarding my payment processing. The date on which I submitted my mortgage payment through the First Citizens mobile application is not the same date the bank appears to be using to credit or apply my payment to my mortgage account. My screenshots clearly show the dates on which my payments were initiated, and those dates do not match the dates reflected by the bank for payment crediting. This discrepancy may have contributed to the erroneous delinquency determination and inaccurate credit reporting. I have included screenshots documenting these inconsistencies. To address these issues, I contacted First Citizens on XX/XX/2026. During that conversation, the customer service representative reviewed my account and specifically informed me that there were no issues with my mortgage account. I was told there were no late charges, no delinquency, and no pending XXXX late credit reporting. The representative instructed me to submit an additional payment of {$97.00} so that my XXXX payment would be considered fully paid and advised that beginning XX/XX/XXXX my new monthly payment amount would become effective. I relied on those representations and believed my account was current. Despite these assurances, First Citizens subsequently reported my mortgage as 30 days past due to the credit reporting agencies. I contacted First Citizens again on XX/XX/2026, seeking an explanation. During that conversation, I was advised that I would receive both a telephone call and a written letter explaining the matter. To date, I have received neither. I have always taken my payment history seriously and have consistently maintained my financial obligations. I do not have a history of making late mortgage payments. I believe the inaccurate credit reporting resulted from multiple servicing errors by First Citizens, including mailing statements to the wrong address, adding an unauthorized curtailment charge without adequate explanation, inconsistently applying or crediting my payments, providing inaccurate information about the status of my account, and failing to properly investigate and resolve my concerns. I have attached copies of my mortgage statements, payment history, screenshots showing the dates my payments were submitted through the mobile application, my credit report reflecting the 30-day late payment, and any additional supporting documentation. I respectfully request that the CFPB require First Citizens Bank to : 1. Conduct a complete investigation of my mortgage account and payment history. 2. Explain why my mortgage statements continued to be mailed to an incorrect address despite my requests to update my mailing address. 3. Provide a detailed written accounting explaining the addition of the curtailment charge and the calculation of my monthly payment. 4. Explain why the payment dates shown in the First Citizens mobile application differ from the dates the bank used to credit my mortgage payments. 5. Explain how my account was determined to be 30 days delinquent despite the payments made and the information provided to me by the banks representative. 6. Correct any servicing or payment application errors on my mortgage account. 7. Remove the inaccurate 30-day late payment from all consumer reporting agencies if the investigation confirms the reporting was erroneous. 8. Provide written confirmation of the investigations findings and all corrective actions taken.

A trade line can not be reported with severe negative collection statuses if the data furnisher fails to supply the actual historical payment data or a verifiable account ledger to justify it. 3. Unlawful Double Reporting and Liability Inflation : XXXX XXXX and LVNV Funding LLC are double-reporting active collection balances for the exact same underlying credit accounts, artificially inflating my debt-to-income liabilities and misrepresenting my credit standing. Capital One Travel is deceptively violating their Price Match Guarantee by refusing to honor prices displayed on websites from a secret internal " banned list, '' even when such listings otherwise meet all eligibility criteria specified in their public terms of service. On XX/XX/year> I booked a hotel using the Capital One Travel portal for USD {$270.00}. Later that same day, I discovered a better price for the same reservation ( same dates, room type, and refund policy ) on XXXX for USD {$220.00}. This rate showed without any special promotion or login. Although XXXX is most frequently a meta-aggregator that searches listings from outside websites, there are * some * listings on XXXX that can be booked by the user entirely within XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ( XXXX takes the user 's payment and sends the booking information to the user upon completion ). The rate I saw on XX/XX/year> was one of these " direct '' bookings with XXXX ( i.e. one that could be completed entirely within XXXX without being redirected to a third party to complete my booking ). As per the terms of the Capital One Travel Price Match Guarantee, I called Capital One Travel at ( XXXX ) XXXX to request a travel credit for the difference in price between the hotel I booked through their portal and the rate I saw on the other public website ( requested credit valued {$48.00} ). The Capital One Travel agent stated that they could not honor my request, as XXXX is on a new internal " banned list '' of websites that Capital One XXXX customer service will never accept for the purposes of the Price Match Guarantee. I confronted the agent with the specific terms of the Price Match Guarantee, asking which part of the terms my XXXX listing violates : " Qualification criteria. To qualify for Capital One Travels price match guarantee, you must keep your original itinerary and the cheaper itinerary found must be : An exact match to the original itinerary that was made within the last 24 hours ( including the cancellation policy, i.e. refundable or non-refundable ) ; Priced in USD, including any taxes and fees ; Available to the general public. For example, this means that the rate doesnt require the customer to log into a site or have a special membership ; Available at the time the customer contacts us. Our agent must be able to verify that the lower price exists. '' ( source : https : //travel.capitalone.com/terms/best-price-guarantee/ ) The agent agreed that the specific reservation I saw on XXXX meets all of the above criteria, but still refused to honor the Price Match Guarantee because XXXX is on their internal " banned list. '' The agent stated that any website on this " banned list '' ( which is not public and * not * mentioned anywhere in the terms of service ) is automatically ineligible for price matching, and that there are no exceptions. Any attempts to reason * why * this booking does not qualify were met with the same circular reasoning ( " because it is banned '' ). After 30 minutes on the phone, a supervisor eventually agreed to offer me a one-time travel credit as a courtesy ( " because this is the first time [ I've ] tried to use the Price Match Guarantee '' ). Nevertheless, the supervisor insisted that any future attempts to price match with XXXX would not be honored. While I am tremendously grateful Capital one made a good faith gesture for the sake of customer service, I am not satisfied that this decision was treated as a one-off courtesy. Whether Capital One Travel likes it or not, there is nothing in the terms of their agreement that excludes otherwise valid listings on XXXX ( or ANY specific website ) from their Price Match Guarantee. This holds especially true for XXXX 's " direct '' bookings, which do not require leaving XXXX and do not list any specific third party vendor. If Capital One Travel wants to operate using a rigid protocol ( a blanket " banned list '' even when all of the specific terms have been satisfied ), this information needs to be in their public terms of service. As it stands, Capital One Travel is misleading consumers by using secret, undisclosed criteria for the Price Match Guarantee instead of only the criteria listed in their public terms of service. To make this right, Capital One needs to stop using private, internal criteria to disqualify Price Match Guarantee requests. That either means 1. stop using a secret " banned list '' altogether or 2. make the existence of such a blacklist public information so consumers can be properly informed * before * a purchase.

creditor believes the account of the obligor was correctly shown in the statement and, upon request of the obligor, provide copies of documentary evidence of the obligors indebtedness. In the case of a billing error where the obligor alleges that the creditors billing statement reflects goods not delivered to the obligor or his designee in accordance with the agreement made at the time of the transaction, a creditor may not construe such amount to be correctly shown unless he determines that such goods were actually delivered, mailed, or otherwise sent to the obligor and provides the obligor with a statement of such determination. After complying with the provisions of this subsection with respect to an alleged billing error, a creditor has no further responsibility under this section if the obligor continues to make substantially the same allegation with respect to such error. ( b ) Billing error For the purpose of this section, a billing error consists of any of the following : ( 1 ) A reflection on a statement of an extension of credit which was not made to the obligor or, if made, was not in the amount reflected on such statement. ( 2 ) A reflection on a statement of an extension of credit for which the obligor requests additional clarification including documentary evidence thereof. ( 3 ) A reflection on a statement of goods or services not accepted by the obligor or his designee or not delivered to the obligor or his designee in accordance with the agreement made at the time of a transaction. ( 4 ) The creditors failure to reflect properly on a statement a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor. ( 5 ) A computation error or similar error of an accounting nature of the creditor on a statement. ( 6 ) Failure to transmit the statement required under section 1637 ( b ) of this title to the last address of the obligor which has been disclosed to the creditor, unless that address was furnished less than twenty days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement is required. ( 7 ) Any other error described in regulations of the Bureau. ( c ) Action by creditor to collect amount or any part thereof regarded by obligor to be a billing error For the purposes of this section, action to collect the amount, or any part thereof, indicated by an obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) does not include the sending of statements of account, which may include finance charges on amounts in dispute, to the obligor following written notice from the obligor as specified under subsection ( a ), if ( 1 ) the obligors account is not restricted or closed because of the failure of the obligor to pay the amount indicated under paragraph ( 2 ) of subsection ( a ), and ( 2 ) the creditor indicates the payment of such amount is not required pending the creditors compliance with this section. Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit any action by a creditor to collect any amount which has not been indicated by the obligor to contain a billing error. ( d ) Restricting or closing by creditor of account regarded by obligor to contain a billing error Pursuant to regulations of the Bureau, a creditor operating an open end consumer credit plan may not, prior to the sending of the written explanation or clarification required under paragraph ( B ) ( ii ), restrict or close an account with respect to which the obligor has indicated pursuant to subsection ( a ) that he believes such account to contain a billing error solely because of the obligors failure to pay the amount indicated to be in error. Nothing in this subsection shall be deemed to prohibit a creditor from applying against the credit limit on the obligors account the amount indicated to be in error. ( e ) Effect of noncompliance with requirements by creditor Any creditor who fails to comply with the requirements of this section or section 1666a of this title forfeits any right to collect from the obligor the amount indicated by the obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) of subsection ( a ) of this section, and any finance charges thereon, except that the amount required to be forfeited under this subsection may not exceed {$50.00}. narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I disgorged more than XXXX unauthorized digitalgoods transactions and several internal transfers were made from my Wells Fargo account. These transactions were not made by me, nor were they authorized by me in any way. The person who made these transactions is a minor family member. She had limited access to my phone only for social media use, not for financial activity. At no point did I give her : My debit card My online banking login Permission to make purchases Permission to make transfers Authorization to access my financial information She accessed my phone without my permission and used my stored payment information to make repeated digitalgoods purchases. I did not know this was happening until I reviewed my account activity and discovered the large number of unauthorized transactions. Upon discovering the fraud, I immediately contacted Wells Fargo and filed a fraud claim. I also filed a police report, and I provided the police report number to Wells Fargo as part of my documentation. Despite the volume of unauthorized transactions, the involvement of a minor, the police report, and the clear lack of authorization, Wells Fargo denied my claim. The stated reason for denial was that the card was in my possession. This reasoning does not reflect the legal definition of unauthorized transactions under Regulation E, which states that unauthorized use occurs when a person initiates a transfer without actual authority, even if they are known to the account holder or have physical access to the device. Wells Fargo closed the investigation without considering : That the person responsible is a minor That she accessed my phone without permission That physical possession of a card does not equal authorization That internal transfers were made without my consent That I provided a police report documenting the fraud That I reported the issue promptly That the pattern of transactions clearly indicates unauthorized use I requested a reinvestigation and escalation. Wells Fargo then forwarded my complaint to their Executive Office, but I am filing with the CFPB because the denial reason is inconsistent with Regulation E protections and does not reflect the facts of the situation. I am requesting that Wells Fargo be required to : XXXX. Reopen and reinvestigate my claim under Regulation E XXXX. Properly evaluate the circumstances of unauthorized access by a minor XXXX. Consider the police report and documentation already provided XXXX. Apply the correct legal standard for unauthorized transactions I am seeking full reimbursement for the unauthorized transactions and transfers. The same minor also made unauthorized transactions on my grandmothers account, which demonstrates a repeated pattern of unauthorized financial activity. narrative: I have a VA-guaranteed mortgage on my primary residence in Florida. While my requests were pending, the servicer continued to add attorney fees and foreclosure-related charges to my account. I have not received an itemization or justification for these fees despite my attempts to resolve the delinquency in good faith. Despite my pending and unanswered repayment plan request, the servicer filed a foreclosure lawsuit against me in Florida. No foreclosure sale has been scheduled. I believe filing foreclosure during a pending loss mitigation review violates 12 CFR 1024.41 ( Regulation X ). I also believe the servicer failed to evaluate me for VA home retention options as required for VA-guaranteed loans before referring the loan to foreclosure. Additionally, the servicer has placed lender-placed ( force-placed ) insurance on my account. The premium being charged is nearly equal to my entire monthly mortgage payment far above the cost of standard homeowner 's insurance. I do not recall receiving the written notices required under 12 CFR 1024.37 before this insurance was charged to my account, including the initial notice at least XXXX days before charging and the required reminder notice. I am unaware of the date the insurance was placed or the basis for the premium amount. My homeowner 's insurance was previously paid through my escrow account, and I believe the servicer allowed that policy to lapse rather than advancing payment as required under 12 CFR 1024.17 ( k ) ( 5 ), and it has refused to allow me to replace the lender-placed coverage.

narrative: XXXX XXXX Bank XXXX : Billing Inquiries/ Disputes XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, OH XXXX RE : Written Notice of Billing Error and Demand for Correction Amount in Dispute : {$2800.00} in interest charges To Whom It May Concern : This is a formal written notice of a billing error under the Fair Credit Billing Act, 15 U.S.C. 1666, and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. I am disputing interest charges assessed to the above account beginning with the statement closing XX/XX/XXXX and continuing through the statement closing XX/XX/XXXX. These charges are the result of a promotional deferred-interest plan being removed from my account without my knowledge, request, or consent. I am requesting that you investigate this matter, correct the error, credit all improperly assessed interest to my account, and provide me with a written explanation and corrected statements as required by law. This notice is submitted under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z, and it independently asserts a breach of the promotional plan agreement and rights under applicable Colorado law. Because XXXX continues to assess improper interest in each successive billing cycle, every monthly statement constitutes a new and separately disputable billing error ; this notice is therefore timely as to each statement within the applicable period, including the most recent statements, and is not limited to the first statement on which the error appeared. To the extent any portion of these charges is asserted to fall outside the XXXX dispute window, the remaining grounds belowbreach of contract, XXXX own admission, and state consumer-protection lawindependently support full correction and refund. XXXX. The Promotional Plan as Originally Established On XX/XX/XXXX, a purchase ( a medical procedure ) of {$7500.00} was made and placed on a promotional credit plan identified on my statements as Plan XXXX, described as XXXX XXXX XXXX INT XXXX XXXX ; that is, No Interest If Paid In Full Within 24 Months. Per the plan terms printed on my own statements, interest would be charged from the purchase date at the purchase APR only if the promotional balance was not paid in full within the promotional period. This is corroborated by the XX/XX/XXXX statement, which lists Plan XXXX with an original purchase amount of {$7500.00}, an original purchase date of XX/XX/XXXX, a New Plan Balance of {$7200.00}, and critically, a Balance Subject to Interest Rate for Purchases of {$0.00} and an Interest Charge of {$0.00}. The XX/XX/XXXX statement again reflects the plan in effect and an XXXX XXXX on Purchases of {$0.00}. In other words, for as long as the plan was correctly in place, no interest was billed. That is exactly how a deferred-interest plan is supposed to function. XXXX. The Unauthorized Removal of the Plan Sometime between the XX/XX/XXXX statement and the XX/XX/XXXX statement, the promotional plan was removed from my account. I did not request this. I did not consent to it. I received no notice of it. The XX/XX/XXXX statement demonstrates the change on its face : the promotional plan section that had appeared on prior statements is gone ; for the first time, the entire purchases balance of {$6500.00} is shown as Balance Subject to Interest Rate at the XXXX XXXX XXXX of 31.99 % ; and an Interest Charge on Purchases of {$170.00} was assessed. A balance that was contractually deferred and not accruing current interest was, without authorization, converted into an ordinary interest-bearing balance. The {$170.00} charge on the XXXX statement is the first dollar of harm. XXXX. XXXX Own Partial Correction Confirms the Error The XX/XX/XXXX statement contains direct evidence that the removal was an error because Comenity itself partially reversed it. A transaction dated XX/XX/XXXX labeled * FINANCE CHARGE * PURCHASES REFUND credits the account - {$340.00}. That figure is the exact sum of the XXXX interest charges wrongly assessed in XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX ( {$170.00} + {$170.00} = {$340.00} ). Transactions dated XX/XX/XXXX labeled PROMOTIONAL PLAN TRANSFER CREDIT ( - {$6900.00} ) and PROMOTIONAL PLAN TRANSFER ( + {$6900.00} ) re-placed the balance onto a new XXXX deferred-interest plan, XXXX, with a plan expiration of XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX therefore acknowledged the mistake, refunded the first XXXX months of interest, and restored a deferred plan. This conduct is an admission that the balance should not have been bearing interest. Having already corrected the same error once, XXXX has both acknowledged the error and established the appropriate remedy : refund of the interest and restoration of the deferred plan. XXXX. The Error Was Not Fully Corrected ; Interest Resumed Improperly Despite the XX/XX/XXXX restoration of a XXXX deferred plan running to XX/XX/XXXX, the very next statement reversed course again. Beginning with the XX/XX/XXXX statement, the purchases balance of {$5800.00} was once more shown as fully subject to interest at 31.99 %, and an XXXX XXXX of {$150.00} was assessed. The deferred periods disclosed on my statements had not arrived, and the improper interest has continued to accrue month after month, now totaling more than XXXX years of charges. XXXX. Amounts in Dispute The following interest charges are disputed in full. Each figure is taken directly from the Interest Charge on Purchases line of the corresponding statement : Statement Closing Interest Charged Note XX/XX/XXXX {$170.00} Refunded by Comenity XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX {$170.00} Refunded by Comenity XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX {$0.00} Refund posted ; plan restored XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$160.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$130.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$130.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$140.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$130.00} Total charged {$3100.00} Less amounts already refunded ( {$340.00} ) Net interest still owed {$2800.00} XXXX acknowledge Comenitys {$340.00} reversal in XX/XX/XXXX. The remaining {$2800.00} in interest, assessed from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, has not been refunded and is improper for the same reason the refunded charges were : the balance was subject to a deferred-interest promotional plan and should not have accrued current interest. Interest continues to be improperly assessed each month this matter remains unresolved. XXXX. Comenitys XX/XX/XXXX Letter Is Not an Investigation of My Complaint Comenity sent me a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX purporting to respond to my concerns. That letter does not constitute an investigation of the complaint I raised, and it does not satisfy Comenitys obligations under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z, for the following reasons. The letter answers a question I never asked. I did not ask XXXX to review, explain, or justify the XX/XX/XXXX refund transaction. I am not disputing the refund ; I welcomed it, and I have credited it against the amount I claim. The XX/XX/XXXX letter addresses only that refund and treats the matter as though my inquiry concerned whether the refund was proper. It did not. By responding to a question I never posed, Comenity has not engaged with my actual complaint at all. The actual complaint remains uninvestigated. My complaint is, and has always been, that the deferred-interest promotional plan was removed from my account without my knowledge, request, or consent, and that current interest has been assessed against a balance that was contractually entitled to deferred treatment. The XX/XX/XXXX letter does not address any of the dispositive questions : when the promotional plan was removed, why it was removed, who authorized its removal, what authorization ( if any ) XXXX relied upon, why a deferred plan running through XX/XX/XXXX was again converted to an interest-bearing balance only XXXX statement after Comenity itself XXXX it, and why interest has continued to accrue every month since. A response that is silent on every XXXX of these questions is not an investigation of the complaint. The letter does not meet the legal standard for a billing-error resolution. Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 and 12 C.F.R. 1026.13, a creditor must conduct a reasonable investigation of the error actually asserted and either correct it or provide a written explanation of why no error occurred, supported by documentary evidence on request. Reframing my dispute as a refund inquiry and answering that substituted question does not discharge that duty. A reasonable investigation must respond to the error the consumer identified, not to a more convenient XXXX of the creditors choosing. Accordingly, I do not accept the XX/XX/XXXX letter as a resolution of this dispute, and I do not regard it as the written investigation and explanation the law requires. The complaint set out in this notice stands unanswered, and the relief demanded below remains outstanding. XXXX. Relief Demanded I request that Comenity Capital Bank : ( a ) Conduct a reasonable investigation of this billing error as required by 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ) and 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( c ) ( f ) ; ( b ) Credit my account in the amount of {$2800.00}, representing all interest assessed from the XX/XX/XXXX statement through the XX/XX/XXXX statement ( or, in the alternative, credit the full {$3100.00} if your records do not reflect the prior {$340.00} reversal ), together with any further interest assessed after the date of this letter ; ( c ) Restore the deferred-interest promotional treatment to which the balance is entitled through its disclosed expiration dates, and cease assessing current interest on the deferred balance ; ( d ) Correct all affected statements and provide me corrected copies ; and ( XXXX ) Provide a written explanation identifying when and why the promotional plan was removed, and the authorization, if any, on which Comenity relied. XXXX. Additional Legal Grounds and Escalation In addition to the Fair Credit Billing Act, my claim rests on independent grounds that are not subject to the Acts dispute-notice timing rules. The promotional plan terms disclosed on my statements form a binding agreement ; by assessing current interest on a balance entitled to deferred treatment before any disclosed expiration date, XXXX has breached that agreement, and I am entitled to restoration of the bargained-for terms and a refund of interest charged in violation of them. The recurring assessment of improper interest on each statement also constitutes an unfair or deceptive practice under the Colorado XXXXonsumer Protection Act and an improper finance charge under the Colorado Uniform Consumer Credit Code. Comenitys XX/XX/XXXX refund and plan restoration are an admission that these charges were improper. I would prefer to resolve this directly. If Comenity does not correct the error and credit the disputed interest within the time federal law allows, I intend to pursue all available remedies. These include filing complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, and the Colorado Attorney Generals office, and pursuing the contractual and statutory claims described above, including recovery of any interest, costs, and attorneys fees permitted by law. I am keeping a complete record of my statements and of all correspondence in this matter, including Comenitys JXX/XX/XXXX letter. XXXX. Your Obligations Under Federal Law You must acknowledge this notice in writing within 30 days of receipt and resolve the dispute within XXXX billing cycles ( and in no event later than 90 days ). During the investigation, you XXXX not collect the disputed amount or any related interest, may not report the disputed amount as delinquent to any credit reporting agency, and may not restrict my account solely because of this dispute. If you determine no error occurred, you must explain that determination in writing and provide copies of documentary evidence on my request. A creditor that fails to comply with these requirements forfeits its right to collect the disputed amount and related finance charges, up to the limit set by 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( e ), and may be liable for statutory damages, costs, and attorneys fees under 15 U.S.C. 1640.

Subject : Request for Investigation Refusal to Cash Valid Check and Potential Discriminatory Treatment To Whom It May Concern, I am requesting a formal investigation into Wells Fargo 's handling of a transaction involving a check that I personally wrote to a XXXX who had completed work at our home. On XX/XX/XXXX, during a period when outdoor temperatures exceeded XXXX degrees, our XXXX, an XXXX XXXX man, presented our Wells Fargo check ( XXXX XXXX ) for payment at a Wells Fargo XXXX. Rather than verifying the check with us or following what we believed would be standard banking procedures, the branch refused to cash the check and instructed our XXXX to return the check to us and have us contact the bank. At no point during this process did anyone from Wells Fargo attempt to contact us, despite the fact that : We are the account holders for almost XXXX decades. The account contained sufficient funds to cover the check - at any given point, our accounts average between {$25000.00} and {$32000.00}. The check was legitimate and written by XXXX XXXX XXXX. We were readily available by telephone and could have verified the check immediately. Instead, our XXXX was turned away and required to leave the branch without payment for work he had completed. As a result, he was forced to return to our home in extreme heat carrying a check that should have been honored or, at a minimum, verified with us before service was denied. Afterward, we filed a formal complaint with Wells Fargo. Rather than addressing the specific circumstances of what occurred, we received a generic form letter stating only that " banking procedures were followed. '' The response did not identify : What specific procedure was followed, Why was the check refused, Why no effort was made to contact us, Or why our XXXX was instructed to return to us, rather than the bank performing even the most basic verification. This response failed to answer any of the questions we raised. Because our XXXX is XXXX XXXX, and because of Wells Fargo 's well-documented history of discrimination and disparate treatment involving minority customers, we are deeply concerned that race may have played a role in how he was treated. We recognize that we can not determine the reason for the bank 's actions, which is precisely why we are requesting an independent investigation. We respectfully request that investigators determine : Why was the check refused despite sufficient funds being available? Why did Wells Fargo fail to contact us before denying payment? What policies or procedures were relied upon? Whether those procedures were applied consistently and without regard to race. Whether similarly situated customers presenting comparable checks receive different treatment. We also request that Wells Fargo preserve and review all records relating to this transaction, including : teller notes, branch manager notes, fraud or verification flags, transaction logs, surveillance video, and any internal documentation explaining why the check was not honored. As customers, we expect Wells Fargo to treat every individual fairly and professionally. We also expect legitimate concerns to receive meaningful responses rather than generic form letters that fail to address the issues raised. Our purpose in filing this complaint is not simply to seek an explanation for this one incident but to ensure that no customer or XXXX is subjected to unnecessary barriers or potentially disparate treatment in the future. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

I am filing this complaint against PNC Bank for what appears to be a systemic and deceptive practice of blocking legitimate, high-value outbound external transfers to prevent customers from liquidating or closing their accounts. This issue is not isolated, as I have observed identical patterns affecting others, indicating a deliberate operational strategy by the bank rather than a routine security measure. The pattern of misconduct is clear : when a customer attempts to transfer a significant portion of their balance out of PNC, the bank abruptly freezes the transfer. Customers are then forced into an endless loop of superficial verification processes through the banks customer service channels that systematically fail to resolve the hold. This intentional delay forces customers to bear an expensive opportunity cost while PNC continues to hold and benefit from the customer 's capital in bad faith. During my most recent attempt to execute an external transfer, PNC representatives provided entirely contradictory and shifting pretexts to justify the freeze : First, I was told on a customer service call that my outbound transfer was blocked because my phone number was unverified. Yet, on that exact same call, representatives successfully used that very phone number to verify my identity. When confronted with this contradiction, the representative shifted the excuse, claiming the number was not verified specifically for external transfers. After completing that secondary verification on the spot, the hold was still not lifted. Finally, the bank changed its narrative again, blaming the hold on " expired documentation. '' PNC had never previously communicated any document deficiencies to me ; this issue was only manufactured and weaponized the moment I attempted to transfer my funds out of the institution. While I am fully willing and able to upload any required documentation digitally, PNC is refusing to resolve this unless I visit a physical branch in person. This requirement is highly obstructive, punitive, and completely unfeasible as I am currently traveling out of state for an internship. PNC Bank is engaging in predatory retention tactics, leveraging fabricated compliance hurdles to restrict access to my consumer funds.
