narrative: To Whom It May Concern : I am filing this complaint against Portfolio Recovery Associates , LLC ( " PRA '' ) regarding its handling of an alleged debt identified as account number ending XXXX, originally issued by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. This complaint concerns XXXX distinct but related violations : ( XXXX ) PRA 's failure to provide debt validation as required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), and ( XXXX ) the furnishing of materially inconsistent and inaccurate information to all three nationwide consumer reporting agencies in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). XXXX. Failure to Validate Debt Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1692g of the FDCPA, I submitted a written request to Portfolio Recovery Associates , LLC disputing the validity of this debt and demanding verification. PRA has failed to provide documentation sufficient to substantiate the debt, including the original account agreement, a complete chain of assignment from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, and an accurate accounting of the balance claimed. Under the FDCPA, a debt collector that fails to validate a disputed debt is barred from continuing collection activity, including continued furnishing of the debt to consumer reporting agencies, until proper validation is provided. XXXX. Materially Inconsistent Reporting Across All XXXX Credit Bureaus Separately, I submitted written disputes directly to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding this same account. XXXX XXXX investigation response to me stated that the information had been " verified as accurate. '' However, a side- by-side review of my credit reports from all three bureaus, generated on or around XX/XX/XXXX, reveals reporting so inconsistent that it can not all be accurate, which calls into serious question whether a reasonable reinvestigation was actually performed as required under FCRA 1681i and whether PRA is furnishing consistent, verifiable data as required under FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ). Specifically : Conflicting account status : XXXX reports this account as " Collection/Charge-Off '' under a " Debt Buyer '' account type. XXXX by contrast, reports the same account as an " Open Account '' in good standing, and XXXX XXXX own Collections summary affirmatively states that I currently have no collections on my credit file. XXXX XXXX credit profile summary shows XXXX delinquent accounts and XXXX derogatory accounts. A single account can not simultaneously be an open, current XXXX XXXX account and a charged-off XXXX-party collection account. Conflicting balances : The balance for this account is reported as {$500.00} on Experian 's account detail page, {$500.00} across a bureau-comparison summary, and reflected within a {$210.00} total balance figure on XXXX XXXX credit profile summary. These figures can not be reconciled to a single, accurate balance. Conflicting account-opening dates : XXXX and the associated account record list the date opened as XX/XX/XXXX, while XXXX XXXX summary lists the oldest account ( the same Portfolio Recovery Associates account ) as opened XX/XX/XXXX a discrepancy that indicates the tradelines were not furnished from a single, consistent source record. Improper account identification : XXXX is displaying this tradeline under a XXXX XXXX account identifier rather than a Portfolio Recovery Associates collection account number, raising the possibility that the original creditor tradeline was not properly updated, suppressed, or merged upon assignment/sale to the collection agency, potentially resulting in duplicate or re-aged reporting of the same underlying debt. No verifiable Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ) : None of the XXXX credit reports display a Date of First Delinquency for this account. The XXXX determines the seven-year period during which a collection account may lawfully be reported under FCRA 1681c. Without a verified DOFD, I am unable to confirm whether this account is being reported within the legally permissible timeframe or has been improperly re- aged. Deleted inquiries coinciding with disputed verification : My XXXX report shows multiple Portfolio Recovery Associates inquiries that were removed as " deleted '' from my credit file at or around the same time the underlying tradeline was represented as " verified and updated. '' The removal of related inquiries while the account itself was simultaneously certified as accurate undermines confidence that a substantive, good-faith investigation was conducted. Gaps in payment history data : The XXXX payment history for this account shows " No Data '' ( ND ) entries in the midst of an otherwise continuously coded collection history, which is itself inconsistent with accurate month-by-month furnishing. XXXX. Requested Relief I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : Investigate Portfolio Recovery Associates , LLC 's failure to validate this debt as required under the FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and its continued reporting of the account during the pendency of an unresolved validation request. Investigate PRA 's furnishing practices under FCRA 1681s-2, given the documented inconsistencies in account status, balance, and account-opening date reported to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Require PRA and/or the credit reporting agencies to produce complete supporting documentation for this account, including the chain of assignment, a verified Date of First Delinquency, and the basis for the conflicting status designations, or, absent such documentation, to delete this tradeline from all three credit reports. Require correction of this tradeline so that identical, accurate information is reported consistently across all three nationwide consumer reporting agencies, as required under the FCRA. Supporting documentation, including screenshots of my XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX credit reports showing the discrepancies described above, is attached to this complaint as exhibits. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am available to provide any additional documentation the Bureau may require

I am filing this formal complaint against Bank of America due to an abrupt administrative account closure that has caused severe consumer harm, immediate financial hardship, and a loss of contractual promotional opportunity. I immediately went to a physical branch and offered to present multiple forms of valid government identification and proof of address to manually verify my identity. The bank flatly refused to accommodate an in-person verification, stating that they could not halt or cancel the liquidation process, and that my entire account balance was locked up in a paper cashier 's check sent via standard USPS mail . By freezing my liquid capital and forcing a multi-week delay via snail mail, Bank of America has placed me in an immediate financial hardship. While my major fixed bills are currently covered, the banks refusal to disburse my funds in-branch has cut off my daily liquidity, leaving me actively struggling to cover essential living expenses, specifically groceries for my household and fuel to commute to work. This is a direct example of severe and avoidable consumer harm caused by an unyielding, automated corporate process. Furthermore, Bank of America 's premature closure directly disrupted a binding promotional contract. Upon opening this account, I enrolled in a sign-up promotion offering a cash bonus of up to {$500.00} for establishing {$10000.00} or more in qualifying direct deposits within XXXX days. As proven by my verifiable financial records, I had already successfully initiated and established recurring qualifying deposits, including {$2200.00} in monthly rental property income and approximately {$1100.00} in monthly XXXX housing allowance, alongside a biweekly employment payroll deposit of {$1600.00}. Over the XXXX window, my guaranteed direct deposits were on track to total nearly $ XXXXeasily clearing the bank 's {$10000.00} threshold. By abruptly shutting down the account before these finalized deposits could clear, Bank of America unilaterally breached the spirit of our agreement and directly denied me the opportunity to earn the {$500.00} bonus I was actively on track to satisfy.

narrative: I am filing this complaint because Santander Consumer USA has once again improperly serviced my simple interest auto loan despite previously acknowledging this exact issue in response to an earlier CFPB complaint. This is now the second time Santander has processed one of my payments in the same manner, requiring me to contact customer service and file another complaint. Santander 's payment history shows that the payment was applied as follows : {$500.00} applied to accrued interest {$990.00} applied to principal Despite applying more than {$500.00} of my payment toward accrued interest, Santander continued to show my next payment due on XX/XX/2026, as though my scheduled payment had not been satisfied. I first attempted to resolve this matter through Santander 's online chat. The representative incorrectly informed me that my payment had been applied as a principal payment. This statement is contradicted by Santander 's own payment history, which clearly shows that {$500.00} of my payment was applied to interest. I then contacted Santander by telephone. The representative again provided incorrect information by stating that any payment made before the due date is automatically considered a principal payment. That explanation is inconsistent with how Santander actually applied my payment, because a principal-only payment would not have included a deduction for accrued interest. This is the exact same servicing issue that resulted in my previous CFPB complaint. In Santander 's written response to my prior CFPB complaint, Santander acknowledged that : My loan is a simple interest loan. Payments are first applied to accrued interest and then to principal. Santander intentionally does not advance the payment due date when an early payment is made unless the customer specifically contacts Santander and requests that the due date be advanced. This is a way for Santander to drag the loan out and collect as much interest as they possibly can. The interest on my account is 29.99 %. After my previous complaint, Santander manually corrected my account and advanced my due date. Despite that prior complaint and correction, Santander repeated the exact same servicing practice again on my XX/XX/2026, payment, forcing me to spend additional time contacting customer service and once again seeking assistance through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. I believe Santander 's servicing practice is confusing and misleading to consumers. Santander deducts accrued interest from early payments while simultaneously refusing to advance the payment due date unless the customer specifically requests that adjustment. A reasonable consumer who sees interest deducted from a payment could believe that the scheduled payment obligation has been satisfied. I am also concerned that this servicing practice has the effect of increasing the amount of interest consumers ultimately pay over the life of their loans. Because Santander continues to require another payment on the original due date unless the borrower requests otherwise, borrowers who are unaware of Santander 's internal policy may unknowingly pay additional interest that could have been avoided had their payments been serviced differently. This issue should not require repeated customer complaints and repeated CFPB complaints to obtain proper servicing of an account. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate Santander 's payment servicing practices, including whether consumers are being provided clear and accurate disclosures regarding how early payments on simple interest loans are applied and whether Santander 's practices comply with applicable consumer protection laws. I also request that Santander : Correct my account and properly advance my payment due date consistent with the servicing correction made after my previous CFPB complaint. Provide a detailed written explanation of how my XX/XX/2026, payment was applied. Explain why customer service representatives continue providing inaccurate and contradictory explanations regarding the application of payments on simple interest loans. Review whether Santander 's policies regarding early payments are misleading to consumers and whether those policies result in unnecessary interest charges. Attached are copies of : Santander 's payment history showing {$500.00} applied to interest and {$990.00} applied to principal from my XX/XX/2026, payment. My account showing that my due date remains XX/XX/2026, despite that payment. My communications with Santander attempting to resolve the issue. Santander 's prior CFPB response acknowledging its policy and confirming that it manually corrected my account after my previous complaint. Thank you for your review of this matter.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint as a follow-up to CFPB Complaint No. XXXX and Capital One XXXX XXXX. XXXX regarding a disputed transaction involving XXXX XXXX / XXXXXXXX XXXX in the amount of {$87.00}. My concern is not only the merchants conduct, but Capital Ones decision to reverse the provisional credit after receiving the merchants response while appearing to evaluate this matter solely as a cancellation-policy dispute rather than considering the actual circumstances that gave rise to the dispute. The original purchase was made on XX/XX/XXXX for a discounted promotional kayaking excursion voucher. Because of the age of the transaction by the time the scheduled excursion occurred, I was unable to pursue a traditional dispute through normal channels and ultimately sought assistance through my original CFPB complaint. Following that complaint, Capital One opened a dispute investigation and issued a temporary credit for the disputed transaction, as well as related fees and interest charges. Capital One then contacted the merchant for a response. After receiving the merchants response, Capital One rebilled the disputed amount to my account and informed me that the case would be considered closed unless I provided additional information by XX/XX/XXXX. I am disappointed in Capital Ones decision to reverse the provisional credit based upon the merchants response, particularly because the merchants rebuttal focused almost entirely on the existence of a refund policy and the assertion that the tour was not cancelled, while largely ignoring the circumstances that actually caused the dispute. I am equally disappointed that after Capital One invited me to continue the dispute, I was informed that I would either need to mail documentation or call to obtain a secure upload link in order to submit additional information. Rather than providing a direct and accessible method for continuing the dispute online, I was required to take additional steps simply to provide the information Capital One requested. Therefore, I am submitting the requested information through this CFPB complaint and attaching all supporting documentation. This dispute did not arise because I simply changed my mind about attending a tour or later decided I wanted a refund despite a refund policy. I traveled from out of town specifically for this excursion and incurred lodging, fuel, food, travel, and planning expenses in order to participate. Upon arrival for the scheduled excursion, I encountered a completely different situation than the one later portrayed by the merchant. I arrived around XXXX minutes before the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX check-in time, as many reasonable and responsible customers would for a guided outdoor excursion on XXXX XXXX that theyve travelled a good distance to attend. When I arrived, the building was locked. No guide was present. No management representative was present. There was no organized check-in process. There was no communication regarding equipment, launch procedures, guest instructions, or whether the excursion was even operating. It was an abandoned rendezvous location. Over the next twenty-plus minutes, additional guests continued arriving while confusion persisted regarding whether the tour was taking place. Eventually, individuals associated with the operation arrived. When asked what was happening, they stated they were only shuttle drivers and that they had to figure out what was going on. At no point during my presence at the rendezvous location was meaningful information provided regarding who was in charge, what was happening, why normal operations were not occurring, or what guests should expect. The merchant has since attempted to dismiss these concerns by emphasizing that I arrived early and left prior to departure. However, there is a significant difference between a scheduled check-in time and a scheduled launch time occurring at a separate location requiring transportation. I remained at the rendezvous location until approximately XXXX XXXX roughly twenty minutes after the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX check-in time and only ten minutes before the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX launch. During that period, employees repeatedly stated they did not know what was happening and had to figure things out. The shuttle driver specifically dropped off passengers and then parked the shuttle rather than remaining available to transport additional guests or provide information regarding the status of the excursion. Based upon the complete lack of communication, organization, operational leadership, and professionalism displayed by a company responsible for conducting guided excursions on XXXX XXXX, I no longer felt comfortable participating and elected not to proceed. After the incident, I attempted to resolve the matter directly with the merchant. My first communication was submitted through the companys online contact form because that was the only contact method provided to me at the rendezvous location. The individuals present were unable or unwilling to provide direct ownership or management contact information. Regardless of whether those individuals were employees or contractors, I find it unacceptable that a guided outdoor excursion had no management representative available at the check-in location and no meaningful way for customers to contact ownership during active business operations. After receiving no response to my first communication, I sent a second communication directly to the email address provided in an automated email sent later that same evening requesting that I leave a review for an excursion I never attended. Neither communication received a response. In fact, I only learned any details regarding the alleged emergency after the owner publicly responded to my XXXX review. The owner never responded to my direct communications and instead chose to respond publicly while continuing to ignore my attempts to resolve the matter privately. The merchants response to Capital One focused primarily on the argument that the voucher was non-refundable and that I did not cancel pursuant to company policy. However, the merchants own response to the Michigan Attorney General contains several admissions that directly support the concerns I have raised from the beginning. In that response, the merchant admits that the emergency : temporarily impacted normal check-in operations. The merchant further states : communication during the emergency could have been clearer and further admits : We have since reviewed internal procedures to further improve communication protocols during unforeseen events. These admissions are important because they acknowledge operational disruption, communication deficiencies, and the need for procedural review and improvement after the incident. The owner simultaneously argues that I should accept responsibility while acknowledging that communication procedures required improvement and that normal check-in operations were impacted. If communication protocols required review and improvement afterward, then there was clearly a communication breakdown during the event itself. That communication breakdown is the very issue I have consistently raised from the beginning and the primary reason I lost confidence in participating. The merchants abbreviated submission to Capital One largely omitted these admissions and instead framed the matter as a simple refund-policy dispute. My concern is that Capital One appears to have accepted that framing. The dispute is not whether a refund policy existed. The dispute is whether the circumstances presented to paying customers at the scheduled check-in location were consistent with the level of communication, organization, professionalism, and operational management reasonably expected of a guided commercial excursion. The merchants own statements acknowledge that they were not. I am therefore requesting that Capital One conduct a fair review of the complete circumstances surrounding this dispute rather than relying solely upon the merchants assertion that no cancellation occurred under company policy. Documents Attached and Submitted in Support of This Complaint XXXX. Original CFPB Complaint No. XXXX Complaint that resulted in Capital One opening a dispute investigation despite the age of the transaction. XXXX. Capital One Case Documentation Capital One Case No. XXXX. Capital One Dispute XXXX XXXX. XXXX. XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX Capital One Dispute Letter Showing Capital One opened the dispute, issued a provisional credit for the transaction, and credited related fees and interest while awaiting the merchants response. XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX Capital One Dispute Letter Showing Capital One reversed the provisional credit after receiving the merchants response and informed me that I would need to either mail documentation or call to obtain a secure upload link in order to continue the dispute. XXXX. Merchant Chargeback Response Submitted to Capital One Including the merchants statements regarding the refund policy, alleged fulfillment of the excursion, and request that the chargeback be reversed. XXXX. Michigan Attorney General Complaint File Including the complaint and closure correspondence. XXXX. Merchant Response Submitted to the Michigan Attorney General Including the merchants admissions that : normal check-in operations were impacted, communication during the incident could have been clearer, and internal procedures were reviewed afterward to improve communication protocols during unforeseen events. XXXX. Follow-Up Email Sent Directly to the Merchant After Initial Contact Attempt Submitted Through the Merchants Online Contact Form Submitted after the incident in an effort to resolve the matter directly with the company. Sent after receiving an automated review request for an excursion I never attended. These attempts at communication went unanswered. XXXX. Public Review and Merchant Response Demonstrating that the merchant chose to respond publicly while failing to respond to direct communications. XXXX. Reservation Confirmation and Reminder Emails Showing the scheduled XXXX XXXX check-in/meet time and XXXXXXXX XXXX launch time. Included because the merchant repeatedly characterizes the issue as my arrival before check-in, despite the fact that I remained at the rendezvous location until approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX, roughly twenty minutes after the scheduled check-in time and only ten minutes before the scheduled launch. These documents demonstrate that check-in and launch were separate events occurring at different times and that customers were expected to arrive before launch in order to complete check-in and transportation arrangements. Collectively, these documents demonstrate that this dispute arose from operational disruptions, communication failures, and the handling of the excursion itselfnot from a simple disagreement regarding a refund policy. My position remains unchanged. Medical emergencies happen. My concern has never been that an emergency occurred. My concern is that paying customers were left without meaningful communication, leadership, organization, or confidence in the operation at the very time they were expected to participate in a guided XXXX XXXX excursion, and that the merchant continues to characterize those concerns as irrelevant while simultaneously admitting that communication and operational procedures required review and improvement afterward. Under these circumstances, I do not believe this matter can be fairly reduced to a simple no refund policy dispute.

narrative: Cedars Business Services ( reference number XXXX, creditor account XXXX ) is attempting to collect an alleged debt of {$1200.00} arising from a purported XXXX parking penalty. I dispute this debt in its entirety. I received Cedars ' initial collection notice on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX ( within the 30-day period under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ) ) I sent Cedars a written dispute via Certified Mail, demanding validation of the debt, including documentation that the debt is valid and legally enforceable in the United States, evidence of Cedars ' authority to collect it, and an explanation of the amount claimed. I retain the Certified Mail receipt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) and 12 C.F.R. 1006.38 ( c ), Cedars was required to cease collection until it mailed me verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment. Cedars has mailed me nothing no verification, no judgment, no response of any kind. Instead, it resumed sending collection notices, most recently on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent a second Certified Mail letter reiterating the dispute and demanding that collection cease ; Cedars has continued regardless. The alleged debt is also not legally collectible. It is a foreign administrative fine. U.S. courts do not enforce foreign penal fines, and California Code of Civil Procedure 1715 ( b ) ( 2 ) expressly excludes fines and penalties from foreign-judgment recognition. No domestic judgment exists. Representing this as a collectible debt misrepresents its legal status in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ), ( 5 ), and ( 10 ), and 1692f ( 1 ), and Cedars ' repeated dunning after a written dispute constitutes harassment under 1692d and 12 C.F.R. 1006.14. I request that the CFPB investigate Cedars ' continued collection of disputed, unvalidated, and legally unenforceable foreign penalties against U.S. consumers. I can provide copies of both Certified Mail letters, mailing receipts, and all collection notices received.

narrative: This complaint references prior CFPB Complaint ID XXXX, filed XX/XX/year> and closed XX/XX/year>. That complaint addressed PayPal 's ten-day notification failure, an incorrect " Item Not Received '' case classification, and unauthorized bank debit attempts on a cancelled same-day sale in which I had initiated a full refund within minutes of receiving payment. PayPal 's own written response to that complaint acknowledged that I " was not notified when the refund first began pulling from your bank account instead of your PayPal balance '' and " was not given a clear opportunity to take action early in the process. '' Despite this written admission, PayPal closed that complaint without correcting the case record, without annotating its internal files, and without addressing the classification. I have been engaged in ongoing written communications with PayPal 's Office of Global Customer Complaints and Advocacy since XX/XX/year>, attempting to resolve the outstanding conditions. Those conditions remain unmet. I am filing this new complaint to document material new adverse actions that have occurred since the closure of the prior complaint, during active engagement with PayPal 's own executive advocacy office. New Adverse Action One Account Block Contradicting PayPal 's Own Policy On XX/XX/year>, my PayPal account was temporarily blocked. I can not pay, send, or withdraw money. This block occurred while active restoration discussions were underway with PayPal 's Office of Global Customer Complaints and Advocacy and while the prior CFPB complaint remained part of the documented record of this matter. PayPal 's own published dispute policy states that during a dispute review, a seller " can continue using your PayPal account as usual. '' My account is fully blocked, in direct contradiction of this stated policy, while two separate dispute cases are simultaneously active and executive-level restoration discussions are ongoing. The block was triggered by PayPal 's automated system at the exact moment an incoming payment of {$1400.00} arrived from a separate transaction on XX/XX/year> not as a result of any action by me, and not as a result of any court order or regulatory directive. New Adverse Action Two Second " Item Not Received '' Classification Arising from PayPal 's Own Platform Design On XX/XX/year>, a buyer named XXXX XXXX paid {$1400.00} through PayPal for a private party sale of audio equipment listed on XXXX XXXX XXXX. Prior to and concurrent with sending the invoice, I had communicated in writing on multiple occasions that PayPal was not an accepted payment method for this sale and that payment via XXXX was required. Specifically : At XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, I stated in writing : " I prefer payment via XXXX. Let me know if that works for you. '' At XXXX XXXX, I sent the invoice. The invoice Special Remarks stated : " Payment via XXXX preferred ; details to follow. '' At XXXX XXXX, prior to any payment notification, I sent a follow-up email explicitly stating : " PayPal may appear as an option on the XXXX invoice , but it is not an option for this sale. '' At XXXX XXXX sixteen minutes after that written exclusion PayPal notified me that {$1400.00} had been received from the buyer. The payment had processed through a default PayPal hyperlink embedded by XXXX XXXX XXXX 's invoice system a link I did not control, did not authorize, and could not remove after the invoice was sent. I immediately contacted the buyer by email and by text message, explained that the payment had been absorbed by PayPal against a pre-existing disputed account balance, that I had received no usable funds, and that I was offering to hold the listing while he requested a PayPal reversal and re-sent payment via XXXX. The buyer did not respond to either contact. Instead, on XX/XX/year>, he filed a PayPal dispute under Case ID XXXX, classified as " Item Not Received. '' The buyer 's own written note to PayPal in that dispute states : " I will not be proceeding with this transaction or this seller off site. I need to cancel this payment or receive a refund. '' He does not allege that goods were shipped and not delivered. He describes a transaction he wishes to cancel. PayPal 's system nonetheless applied the " Item Not Received '' classification the same classification applied in the prior XXXX matter, and the same classification that PayPal 's own prior written admission confirmed was a product of PayPal 's processing architecture rather than any failure by me. No item was shipped. No item will be shipped under these circumstances. Had I been properly informed about all available income-driven repayment options and their potential benefits, I would have had the opportunity to make a more informed decision regarding my repayment. I am also requesting an explanation of why I was not identified as an affected borrower for purposes of the CFPB restitution process and whether my account should be reconsidered for relief based on my servicing history. I would like a written response addressing these concerns and explaining what corrective action, if any, will be taken.

narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Consumer Complaint Subject : Systemic Escrow Mismanagement, Unauthorized Funds Siphoning, Intentional FCRA Reporting Violations, and Illegal Refusal to Recognize a Deceased Borrower Status / Successor in Interest Respondent : Freedom Mortgage Corporation Associated Loan Number : XXXX I. Executive Summary This complaint is filed to formalize a severe, multi-year pattern of systemic administrative failures, gross escrow mismanagement, malicious credit reporting violations, and weaponized corporate incompetence by Freedom Mortgage Corporation. Over consecutive years, Freedom Mortgage has systematically abandoned its fiduciary obligations as an escrow-holding loan servicer. The servicer has failed to timely and fully disburse local property taxes and property insurance premiums, while simultaneously issuing unauthorized, unverified disbursements out of the consumers escrow account. Furthermore, Freedom Mortgage is engaging in a flagrant, multi-layered trap designed to ruin the consumer 's credit standing and prevent them from exiting this loan. The company has weaponized its own approved emergency disaster forbearance to manufacture a legal fiction of delinquency, intentionally misreported a current account as " 30+ days late '' to the credit bureaus, and flatly refused to remove deceased co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX from the loan despite the official submission of her death certificate. When notified of these critical errors via statutory Notices of Error ( NOEs ), Qualified Written Requests ( QWRs ), and internal portal messages, Freedom Mortgage engaged in bad-faith evasion, circular delays, and adversarial customer service. The servicer is actively wielding its own manufactured errors to lock the consumer into an toxic loan structure to maximize its own interest revenue. This predatory corporate paradigm has exacted a profound and quantifiable toll on the consumer 's health, XXXX management, and financial well-being. II. Factual Chronology and Combined Escrow Violations 1. The XXXX Property Tax Failure and Notice of Error As verified in the document " freedom notice of error.pdf '', on XX/XX/XXXX, the consumer, XXXX XXXX, issued a formal statutory Notice of Error ( NOE ) to Freedom Mortgage. The consumer had received an explicit alert from the XXXX XXXX Tax Commissioner stating that a Fieri Facias ( FiFa )/ Tax Lien would be issued against the real property ( located at XXXX XXXX XXXX ) due to unremitted XXXX property taxes. Despite the consumers escrow account showing " Tax Disbursements '' ( including a deduction of {$350.00} on XX/XX/XXXX ), Freedom Mortgage mismanaged the escrow resources, failed to pay the complete billed amount of {$830.00}, and left a delinquent balance of {$350.00} to accrue interest, fees, and penalties. The consumers XXXX explicitly demanded that Freedom Mortgage correct this mismanagement, protect the property from the impending lien, and ensure no fees or interest were assessed to the consumers account. As documented in the file " image.png '', the consumer followed up with Freedom Mortgage regarding the official Lien for FIERI FACIAS recorded on XX/XX/XXXX, in Book XXXX, Page XXXX of Official Records in favor of the City of XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Customer Care issued a response that encapsulates bad-faith evasion : " Please be advised that, upon reviewing your request, Freedom Mortgage is unable to assist you, as the lien referenced in your question is not held by us ; it is held by the City of XXXX. Therefore, we recommend that you directly contact XXXXhe County for further assistance and clarification. '' Freedom Mortgage bypassed the underlying truth : the lien was held by the XXXX of XXXX exclusively because Freedom Mortgage failed to fulfill its statutory obligation to pay the property taxes out of the consumer 's funded escrow account. 2. The Homeowners Insurance Sabotage and Predatory Force-Placed Premium The servicers malicious patterns are further laid bare by a dual-document timeline involving the consumer 's hazard insurance : The Insurance Non-Payment Notice : As verified in the file " XXXX '', the consumers hazard insurance carrier, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ) , issued an urgent status notice for policy XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX regarding mortgage loan XXXX for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX explicitly stated that because Freedom Mortgage failed to collect and remit insurance premiums, XXXX was forced to switch to billing the consumer directly for a balance of {$3000.00}. The Calculated Force-Placed Notice : As verified in the file " XXXX '', on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Mortgage issued a notice to the consumer stating they had force-placed an unnecessary, expensive insurance policy onto the account costing {$2400.00} annually, fraudulently citing a " lack of insurance information. '' This is a textbook example of a predatory servicer trap. Freedom Mortgage defaulted on its obligation to disburse the consumers XXXX hazard insurance premium out of the escrow account, which forced XXXX to drop the mortgage-billing arrangement. Then, Freedom Mortgage weaponized its own failure to pay the existing carrier by fabricating a " lack of insurance information '' to force-place a costly duplicate policy onto the account. 3. Unsubstantiated and Unauthorized Escrow Siphoning The weaponized incompetence of Freedom Mortgage is further demonstrated by completely unauthorized and unverified withdrawals from the consumer 's escrow balance. As documented in " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage issued a " Tax and Insurance Disbursement Confirmation '' for the account ending in XXXX. The confirmation notes that a payment was completed on XX/XX/XXXX to XXXX XXXX XXXX in the amount of {$420.00} for a " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX The consumer has absolutely no knowledge of this disbursement, has received no prior notice or breakdown as to why it was paid, and has never been provided proof of a valid lien associated with this payment by Freedom Mortgage. Freedom Mortgage simply withdrew consumer funds to pay an unverified municipal charge, completely violating basic accounting, verification, and escrow standards. 4. Illegal Refusal to Acknowledge Deceased Status & Successor Options The most egregious display of continuous administrative bad faith is Freedom Mortgage 's complete refusal to update the account following the passing of co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX. The consumer has formally provided and proven through the portal that XXXX XXXX XXXX is deceased by submitting her official death certificate. Despite receiving undeniable legal documentation of her passing, Freedom Mortgage flatly refuses to remove her name from the loan account, refuses to update the loan data fields, and completely ignores requests to provide the legally required Successor in Interest packets, confirmation tracks, or assumptions paths. By pretending a deceased individual is still active while ignoring the living borrower, Freedom Mortgage actively cuts off the legal avenues necessary to modify, restructure, or clean up the loan terms. 5. Weaponized Forbearance, Payment Rollover, and False Credit Reporting A review of files " XXXX '' through " XXXX '' exposes a malicious credit-destroying scheme orchestrated by Freedom Mortgage post-forbearance. The Approved Forbearance : As verified in " XXXX '', on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Mortgage formally approved an emergency disaster Forbearance Plan for the consumer 's loan ( XXXX ), which temporarily suspended monthly mortgage payments from XX/XX/XXXX, through XX/XX/XXXX. The Payment Application Trajectory : As verified in internal messages ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ) and a letter from Supervisor XXXX XXXX ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ), the forbearance period actually remained active from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. During this entire time, the consumer consistently resumed making monthly payments via XXXX. As shown in " XXXX '', an AutoPay payment of {$1200.00} was successfully processed with confirmation XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. The Rolling Delinquency Fraud : In " XXXX '', " XXXX '', and " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage admits in writing that because no payment was made in XX/XX/XXXX ( the exact month covered by their own approved disaster forbearance ), every payment after [ that ] has been applied to the prior month. The Fraudulent Bureau Reporting : Because Freedom Mortgage backward-rolled every single timely post-forbearance payment to the prior month, they created a permanent, artificial one-month lag. They then weaponized this internal accounting fiction to report the consumer to the credit bureaus as " 30 days late '' for XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. As proven by the official credit bureau dispute report in " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage verified this devastating derogatory remark as " accurate '' to the bureaus on XX/XX/XXXX, showing an active " 30 '' day delinquency rating for XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. As the consumer detailed in formal portal disputes ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ) and a executive escalation to Freedom Mortgage XXXX XXXX XXXX ( " XXXX '' ), this practice is completely fraudulent. If a payment was legitimately missing from XXXX, it was legally mandated to be handled within the forbearance framework or reported late in XXXX is an explicit violation of federal law to report a consumer as delinquent in XXXX for a payment that was fully and timely processed on XX/XX/XXXX. III. Statutory Violations and Relevant Legal Precedents Freedom Mortgage 's continuous actions constitute explicit, actionable violations of federal and state consumer protection laws : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) & ( b ) ) : Furnishers are strictly prohibited from reporting information that is inaccurate or materially misleading. Under 1681s-2 ( b ), upon receipt of a dispute, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and delete or correct inaccurate data. Freedom Mortgage willfully verified a patently false " XX/XX/XXXX Delinquency '' to the bureaus despite having processed the consumer 's payment on XX/XX/XXXX. CARES Act & CFPB Bulletin XXXX ( Forbearance Credit Reporting ) : Federal law mandates that if a borrower is granted a forbearance accommodation and resumes payments as scheduled, the servicer must report the account as current. Rolling payments backward to force an artificial delinquency post-forbearance directly subverts the CARES Act. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) / Regulation X ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.17 ( k ) & 1024.30-.41 ) : Freedom Mortgage violated 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( g ) by failing to timely disburse escrow property taxes and XXXX insurance premiums. They additionally violated federal Successor in Interest rules by failing to establish transparent communication tracks, update account records, or provide assumption paths to XXXX XXXX after receiving formal portal notification of co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX ' death. Illegal Assessment of Force-Placed Insurance ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.37 ) : Servicers are prohibited from force-placing hazard insurance unless they have a reasonable basis to believe a borrower 's coverage has lapsed. XXXX has no basis ; the premium breakdown was caused entirely by their own failure to pay XXXX out of the escrow account. Binding Case Law & Enforcement History : 1. Federal Precedent ( XXXX XXXX Freedom Mortgage Corp., XXXX XXXX XXXX ) : Reaffirmed that under RESPA ( 12 U.S.C . 2605 ( g ) ), the obligation to make timely escrow payments is strict, and Freedom Mortgage can not bypass its statutory liabilities when escrowed funds are neglected. 2. Recent Systemic Litigation : Freedom Mortgage faces active litigation for this exact combination of predatory behavior. In XXXX XXXX Freedom Mortgage Corporation ( XXXX. XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ), the servicer was sued for botched escrow calculations and illegally force-placing duplicate hazard insurance overcharges. 3. Documented Regulatory Recidivism : In XX/XX/XXXX, the CFPB penalized Freedom Mortgage Corporation {$3.00} XXXX, with Director XXXX XXXX explicitly labeling them a " repeat offender '' that systemically ignores compliance orders and handles " error-riddled mortgage data. '' Furthermore, in XX/XX/XXXX, the New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs executed a {$500000.00} Consent Order against Freedom Mortgage for violating the Consumer Fraud Act ( CFA ) by failing to timely disburse escrow payments and providing deceptive information to borrowers. Freedom relocated its corporate headquarters from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX, XXXX in the midst of these expanding regulatory investigations into their servicing mechanics. IV. Quantifiable Financial Harm and Impact on Well-Being The Escrow Trap to Enforce Poverty : By mismanaging escrow disbursements, creating artificial title clouds ( the recorded FiFa lien ) , siphoning unverified funds ( {$420.00} municipal withdrawal ) without documentation, fabricating thousand-dollar force-placed insurance charges, ignoring a legal death certificate to freeze the loan 's status, and obliterating the consumer 's credit score via fraudulent " 30-day late '' trended data reporting, Freedom Mortgage has engineered a total financial chokehold. Because a property with an active tax lien, erratic escrow shortages, or locked title status can not satisfy standard underwriting guidelines, Freedom Mortgage uses its own administrative failures to trap the consumer in this loan. This completely blocks the consumer from refinancing into better market terms or exiting the loan, preserving Freedom Mortgage 's interest revenue while systematically keeping the consumer financially suppressed. Profound Health and Emotional Damage : The psychological cost of experiencing years of weaponized corporate incompetence can not be overstated. Constantly defending one 's home against tax foreclosure, fighting circular bureaucratic loops, tracking down unauthorized withdrawals, navigating the emotional toll of a co-borrower 's passing while the servicer uses her death as a bureaucratic stalling tool, and managing severe health XXXX under an environment of constant corporate gaslighting has inflicted a severe, compounding toll on the consumer 's physical and mental health. The chronic stress of dealing with an adversarial institution that actively sabotages your credit and financial health has drastically deteriorated the consumers daily quality of life.

narrative: I am filing this complaint because I believe Wells Fargo failed to investigate an unauthorized electronic fund transfer properly and improperly denied my fraud claim despite my immediate reporting and full cooperation throughout the investigation. On XX/XX/year>, I received a Wells Fargo fraud alert text message and email at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX regarding a suspicious {$140.00} debit card transaction. I immediately contacted Wells Fargo at approximatelXXXX XXXX XXXX to report the suspicious activity. While reviewing my account immediately after that call, I discovered an additional unauthorized {$600.00} transaction that had occurred shortly before the {$140.00} transaction. I immediately called Wells Fargo again at approximately XXXX PM to report the {$600.00} transaction and file a fraud claim. During these conversations, I informed Wells Fargo that my debit card remained physically in my possession. I verified my card number over the phone. I advised the representative that I was in XXXX at the time of the unauthorized transaction, not at the location where the transaction occurred. I did everything a reasonable consumer is expected to do. I reported the fraud within minutes of becoming aware of it, cooperated fully with Wells Fargo, submitted requested information, filed a police report, and have participated in nearly a dozen phone calls attempting to resolve this matter. Despite these facts, Wells Fargo denied my claim. I believe Wells Fargo failed to conduct a reasonable investigation as required under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. ) and Regulation E ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1005 ). My concerns include the following : Wells Fargo 's own fraud monitoring systems identified the {$140.00} transaction as suspicious almost immediately, yet the unauthorized {$600.00} transaction that occurred moments earlier was not afforded the same scrutiny. Wells Fargo has never explained this inconsistency. I repeatedly informed Wells Fargo that I still possessed my physical debit card. During my initial calls, I read the card number directly from the card in my possession. My debit card has a very distinctive sunflower design. If surveillance footage from the ATM or transaction location exists, it could help determine whether the card presented was my original card or a cloned or counterfeit version. I requested that Wells Fargo review or obtain this evidence, but I have not received confirmation that it did so. During a later conversation with a Wells Fargo representative, I was informed that the chip information associated with the transaction may not have been authenticated. Despite this, my claim remained denied. I repeatedly requested documentation explaining why my claim was denied, the evidence Wells Fargo relied upon, and whether surveillance footage, ATM records, or other investigative materials were reviewed. I have not received a meaningful explanation. I specifically asked Wells Fargo whether it investigated the possibility of card skimming, card cloning, counterfeit card activity, or another form of unauthorized access. I have not received an explanation of what investigative steps, if any, were taken. I am also disappointed by Wells Fargo 's overall handling of this matter. When I visited a Wells Fargo branch seeking assistance with my fraud claim, I was presented with offers for pre-approved credit cards rather than receiving meaningful support regarding my dispute. This interaction reinforced my belief that my concerns were not being treated with the seriousness they deserved. The financial impact of this loss has been significant. I am a hardworking single mother, and {$600.00} represents money that should have been available for essential household expenses. More importantly, I believe consumers who promptly report unauthorized transactions should receive a fair and thorough investigation. I am requesting that the CFPB review Wells Fargo 's handling of this claim and determine whether it complied with its obligations under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E. Specifically, I request that Wells Fargo be required to : - Reopen Claim # XXXX. - Conduct a new and independent investigation. - Provide a detailed written explanation of the evidence relied upon in concluding that I authorized the transaction. - Explain whether the transaction was processed using an XXXX chip, magnetic stripe, contactless payment, or another authentication method. - Explain whether Wells Fargo investigated the possibility of card skimming, card cloning, counterfeit card activity, or other unauthorized access. - Confirm whether ATM logs, surveillance footage, merchant records, or other investigative materials were requested or reviewed. - Reimburse the unauthorized {$600.00} transaction if Wells Fargo can not demonstrate that I authorized it. I believe I fulfilled every obligation expected of a consumer by reporting the fraud immediately, maintaining possession of my card, cooperating fully with the investigation, and filing a police report. The continued reporting of these accounts violates FCRA 611 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) and FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) because disputed information must be properly verified before remaining on a consumer report. The furnishers have also failed to comply with FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) because the information being furnished has not been proven accurate or complete, and the credit reporting agencies have failed to maintain maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ) 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). narrative: CRITICAL NOTICE TO INVESTIGATOR AND RESPONDENT : The CFPB electronic portal forces consumers to select from a restrictive list of predefined, automated dropdown categories to submit a form. The consumer has selected the closest available structural option ( " Dispute the Amount '' ) under protest solely to bypass portal formatting constraints.This submission is made strictly as a dispute regarding structural non-compliance, lack of statutory chain of title, and material misrepresentations by the collector. This filing does not constitute a validation of liability, an admission or acknowledgment of any alleged debt instrument, or a waiver of any consumer rights under federal or state law. The consumer reserves all rights to contest the existence, ownership, validity, and enforceability of the alleged balance in its entirety. I am submitting this formal complaint against Second Alliance , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX, CA ) for explicit violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Oregon Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act ( OUDCPA ), and the California Rosenthal Act. The agency is engaging in unlawful continued collection activities and utilizing material misrepresentations to pressure me into an unsafe refinancing agreement. 1. Failure to Provide Mandatory Chain of Title Following an initial communication, Second Alliance , Inc. sent a validation packet containing only an underlying student loan contract executed with XXXX Bank. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I exercised my rights under ORS 646A.670 and sent a formal statutory dispute noticing the deficiency. I demanded physical business recordssuch as an assignment agreement or bill of saleproving a clear, unbroken chain of ownership from the original creditor ( XXXX Bank ) to the current alleged owner. Second Alliance , Inc. failed to produce any physical transfer documentation. 2. False, Deceptive, and Contradictory Ownership Narrative Instead of pausing collection efforts to compile the statutory evidence, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sent a response letter containing a blatant factual and legal impossibility. The letter explicitly states : " The owner and loan holder is and has always been XXXX student loan. XXXX was the originating lender. '' Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e and Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17, debt collectors are strictly prohibited from using false or misleading representations regarding the character or legal status of a debt. An originating lender is, by definition, the first legal owner and holder of a signed promissory note. Therefore, Edly could not have " always '' been the holder. Furthermore, independent credit reporting data directly refutes the agency 's claim. The consumer 's credit profile shows the loan was held under " XXXX '' ( XXXX Bank ) until XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX, moved to " XXXX '' for one month, and was explicitly marked " Transferred to another lender '' in XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX This independent credit data proves that the loan has undergone multiple structural assignments and transfers, making the agency 's written claim of continuous, unbroken ownership a patently false misrepresentation designed to obscure a missing chain of title. 3. Unlawful Continued Collections and Refinancing Solicitation While my statutory validation request remained pending and unfulfilled, Second Alliance , Inc. actively continued collection efforts by attempting to solicit a {$350.00} voluntary payment to " re-age '' the loan. Furthermore, they used this deceptive ownership narrative to push a high-pressure solicitation to " refinance '' the debt through a partner lender. Under Oregon law ( ORS 646.639 ) and California 's Rosenthal Act ( Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17 ), a debt collector must completely cease and freeze all collection efforts upon receiving a consumer dispute until accurate validation is provided. Attempting to maneuver a consumer out of a highly disputable contract with missing ownership records and into a brand-new, refinanced loan agreement before validating the debt constitutes an unfair, deceptive, and abusive collection practice.

Fraudulent accounts and inaccurate reporting accounts have been wrongfully placed on my credit file. These items are not mine and must be permanently deleted and blocked from further reporting. narrative: My name is XXXX XXXX, and I am submitting this formal complaint regarding my recent experience with the World Finance branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, Missouri XXXX. I am requesting that World Finance Corporate, Compliance, and Ethics departments conduct a complete review and investigation into the handling of my personal loan application, the communication surrounding the application process, and the failure to provide me with timely and adequate information regarding the decision made on my application. On or around XX/XX/year>, I submitted an application for a personal loan in the amount of {$12000.00} through the World Finance branch located at the address listed above. I applied in good faith and provided the requested information necessary for the company to evaluate my application, including information relating to my employment, income, identity, and intended use of the requested loan proceeds. I entered into this process expecting a professional and transparent lending experience. I understand that lenders have underwriting requirements and that not every application is approved. However, regardless of the final lending decision, consumers deserve to be treated fairly, communicated with professionally, and provided with appropriate explanations when adverse decisions are made. My concern is not simply that my application was denied. My concern is the manner in which my application was handled, the lack of follow-up communication, the failure to provide the promised callback, and the absence of a clear written explanation regarding the reasons for the denial. Background Regarding My Loan Application After submitting my application, I was contacted by a World Finance representative named XXXX XXXX. During our conversation, XXXX XXXX asked me questions regarding my loan request, including questions about why I wanted the funds and what I intended to use the money for. I explained that the requested funds were for legitimate personal expenses, including repairs and maintenance related to my XXXX XXXX. Specifically, I explained that the funds were needed for necessary vehicle-related expenses, including : New tires ; Brake repairs ; Vehicle sensor repairs ; and Other maintenance-related expenses. I also provided information regarding my employment and income. I explained that I earn approximately {$5700.00} every two weeks. I answered the questions presented to me and fully cooperated throughout the process. I understand that lenders may ask questions regarding loan purpose, income, employment, and financial circumstances as part of their underwriting process. However, during the conversation, I felt that the discussion became unnecessarily focused on questioning my personal financial decisions rather than evaluating my application based on my qualifications and the information provided. I was willing to provide information necessary for the application review process, but I expected the interaction to remain professional, respectful, and focused on the actual lending criteria. Promised Callback That Never Occurred At the conclusion of my conversation with XXXX XXXX, I was specifically advised that he would call me back within approximately one hour regarding the status of my application. Based on that statement, I reasonably expected a follow-up communication regarding whether additional documentation was needed, whether my application required further review, or whether a decision had been made. However, that callback never occurred. I did not receive the promised phone call. I was not contacted by XXXX XXXX to explain the status of my application. I was not informed directly that my application had been denied. Instead, I later learned that my application had been denied without receiving the communication that had been promised to me. This lack of communication was concerning because I had taken the time to provide information, answer questions, and cooperate with the application process. At a minimum, I believe I should have received a professional follow-up explaining the outcome. Failure to Receive Written Explanation of Denial After learning that my loan application was denied, I expected to receive a written explanation identifying the reasons for the decision. As of the date of this complaint, I have not received a written adverse action notice explaining the principal reasons for the denial of my application. A consumer should not be left guessing why a financial decision was made, particularly when that decision affects access to credit. A written explanation is important because it allows consumers to : Understand the basis of the decision ; Correct possible errors ; Address issues affecting future applications ; Determine whether inaccurate information was used ; Exercise applicable consumer rights. Without a written explanation, I have no way of knowing whether the decision was based on : Credit information ; Verification issues ; Income considerations ; Documentation concerns ; Underwriting criteria ; Internal policies ; or Any other factor. I respectfully request that World Finance provide the complete adverse action notice associated with my application, including the principal reasons for the denial. Concerns Regarding Application Handling My concerns regarding this matter include, but are not limited to, the following : 1. Failure to provide promised follow-up communication I was specifically told that I would receive a callback within one hour. That communication never occurred. Consumers should not be told they will receive follow-up communication and then receive no response. 2. Lack of transparency regarding the denial decision I was denied but was not provided with a clear explanation of why the application was declined. A transparent lending process requires that consumers understand the basis for significant financial decisions. 3. Lack of professionalism during the application review While I understand that lenders may ask questions about loan purpose and financial circumstances, I felt the conversation became unnecessarily focused on challenging my personal reasons for requesting the loan rather than objectively reviewing my application. 4. Concern regarding whether proper procedures were followed I am requesting that World Finance review whether the application was processed consistently with company policies and applicable consumer lending requirements. Request for Internal Investigation I respectfully request that World Finance conduct a formal internal investigation into this matter. As part of that investigation, I request review of : My complete loan application file ; The underwriting decision ; The decision timeline ; Internal notes ; Communication records ; Telephone recordings, if available ; Employee notes ; System records ; Any internal messages regarding my application; Any documentation relied upon in making the lending decision. I specifically request that World Finance preserve all records relating to my application while this complaint is under review. This preservation request includes : Call recordings ; Application records ; Underwriting documentation ; Credit decision records ; Internal communications ; Emails ; Text messages ; Employee notes ; Time stamps showing application review activity ; Approval or denial records. Request for Complete Loan File Documentation I respectfully request copies of all documents associated with my application, including : Application submission records ; Documents provided during the application process ; Verification records ; Underwriting notes ; Decision records ; Adverse action notice ; Reason codes ; Any communications related to the denial. Providing these records will allow me to better understand the decision-making process and determine whether any errors occurred. Fair Lending Concerns I want to make clear that I am requesting an investigation into the handling of my application and the consistency of the process. I am not making unsupported conclusions regarding the reason for the denial. However, I believe it is appropriate for World Finance to review whether my application was handled consistently with the treatment of similarly situated applicants. If any factor other than legitimate underwriting criteria influenced the handling of my application, I request that World Finance identify and address that issue. A fair lending review should examine whether : Similar applications were evaluated using consistent standards ; The same documentation requirements were applied ; Communication procedures were followed consistently ; The decision was based on legitimate lending factors. Request for CFPB Review I am also submitting this matter to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) because I believe additional oversight is appropriate due to : Lack of communication after the promised callback ; Failure to provide a clear explanation of the denial ; Concerns regarding transparency in the lending process ; The inability to understand what factors resulted in the adverse decision. I respectfully request that the CFPB assist in obtaining : A copy of the adverse action notice ; An explanation of the denial ; Confirmation that proper procedures were followed ; A review of whether the application was handled fairly. Request for Missouri Division of Finance Review I am requesting that the Missouri Division of Finance review this matter to determine whether World Finance followed applicable Missouri lending requirements and consumer protection standards. My concern is not that a lender declined my application. My concern is that the process lacked transparency and communication. Consumers deserve : Clear communication ; Professional treatment ; Accurate information ; Proper documentation ; An explanation of adverse decisions. Requested Resolution To resolve this matter, I respectfully request that World Finance : Conduct a complete investigation into the handling of my loan application. Review all available call recordings and employee notes related to my conversation with XXXX XXXX. Provide a copy of my complete loan application file. Provide the written adverse action notice explaining the principal reasons for the denial. Explain the specific factors that resulted in the denial of my {$12000.00} loan application. Confirm whether my application was reviewed according to standard underwriting procedures. Preserve all records related to my application. Provide a written response detailing the findings of the investigation. Correct any errors identified during the review process. Ensure that future applicants receive appropriate communication regarding application decisions. Conclusion I respectfully request that World Finance take this complaint seriously and conduct a meaningful review of what occurred. I understand that lenders have the right to approve or deny applications based on legitimate underwriting standards. My concern is not simply the denial itself. My concern is the lack of transparency, the failure to provide the promised callback, the lack of communication regarding the decision, and the absence of a written explanation allowing me to understand why my application was declined. I made a good-faith effort to provide accurate information, cooperate with the application process, and answer all questions presented to me. I believe I deserve the same level of professionalism and transparency in return. I respectfully request a written response explaining the results of your investigation and providing the requested documentation. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your timely response.

Per Section 2 and 5.1 of the signed Service Agreement, the program explicitly promises access to weekly coaching calls for mentorship, feedback, and accountability, and strictly requires the consumer to attend at least 15 live coaching calls to remain eligible for the program 's performance guarantee. However, as documented in the attached exhibits, the merchant routinely scheduled these mandatory live coaching sessions at approximately XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX on weekdays. I promptly requested cancellation from the merchant due to this lack of performance and accessibility, which they rejected. I then contacted Clarity Pay multiple times to formally dispute the account and request an administrative freeze. I am filing this complaint regarding an ongoing mortgage servicing and escrow accounting dispute with Rocket Mortgage that has remained unresolved despite repeated attempts to resolve the matter directly with the company. In XX/XX/XXXX, Rocket Mortgage, the servicer of my mortgage loan, paid my property taxes from my escrow account as required. However, they also mistakenly paid the property taxes for eight unrelated properties using funds from my escrow account. In XX/XX/XXXX, Rocket Mortgage again used my escrow funds to pay property taxes for an additional seven unrelated properties. Rocket Mortgage representatives have acknowledged this servicing error during multiple telephone conversations and advised me that refund requests were submitted to XXXX XXXX to recover the improperly disbursed funds. As a result of these erroneous tax payments, Rocket Mortgage has repeatedly performed escrow analyses showing significant escrow shortages and has attempted to substantially increase my monthly mortgage payment based on those shortages. Throughout this process, I have remained current on my mortgage, continued making every required monthly payment, including all escrow contributions, and have never defaulted on my loan. Since the dispute began, I have spent countless hours communicating with Rocket Mortgage in an effort to correct errors that were not caused by me. During XXXX, I have continued paying into my escrow account while this matter has remained unresolved. Rocket Mortgage has informed me that only two of the erroneous tax payments have been refunded. However, despite repeated requests, the company has not provided documentation identifying : * Every erroneous tax payment made from my escrow account. * The total amount improperly disbursed. * The total amount recovered. * The amount that remains outstanding. * Documentation showing that refunds received have been credited back to my escrow account. * Documentation showing how my ongoing escrow contributions have been applied. I have also been unable to reconcile the balance of my escrow account because my monthly mortgage statements reflect one escrow balance while my online Rocket Mortgage account displays an escrow balance of {$0.00}. Rocket Mortgage has been unable to explain this discrepancy or provide documentation supporting the actual balance of my escrow account. On XX/XX/XXXX, after months of unsuccessful attempts to obtain this information by telephone, I sent Rocket Mortgage a formal Notice of Error and Request for Information by certified mail requesting a complete escrow accounting, supporting documentation, preservation of records, and a full reconciliation of my escrow account. The notice was delivered on XX/XX/XXXX. During a phone call on XX/XX/XXXX, I was advised that Rocket Mortgage could not provide documentation showing how refunds o r escrow funds were being allocated until all outstanding refunds had been received. I respectfully request that Rocket Mortgage : * Conduct a com plete investigation of my escrow account. * Provide a transaction-by-transaction accounting of every escrow deposit, disbursement, adjustment, refund, credit, debit, and transfer from XX/XX/XXXX, through the present. * Identify every tax parcel and property that received funds from my escrow account. * Identify the total amount improperly disbursed, the total amount recovered, and the amount that remains outstanding. * Provide documentation showing that all refunds received have been credited to my escrow account. * Provide documentation showing that my escrow contributions made during XXXX have been properly credited. * Explain why my mortgage statements and online account display different escrow balances. * Correct any inaccurate escrow analyses and remove any escrow shortages resulting from Rocket Mortgage 's servicing errors. * Provide written confirmation that my escrow account has been fully reconciled and accurately reflects all escrow deposits, refunds, disbursements, and adjustments. I have attempted in good faith to resolve this matter directly with Rocket Mortgage for approximately seven months. Despite repeated assurances that the issue was being addressed, I have not received a complete accounting of my escrow funds or a reconciliation of my account. I respectfully request the CFPB 's assistance in ensuring that Rocket Mortgage properly investigates this matter, provides a complete accounting of my escrow funds, corrects any servicing errors, and restores my escrow account to its proper balance.

I am submitting this complaint regarding Freedom Mortgage Corporations handling of my FHA mortgage loss-mitigation application, its inaccurate or misleading characterization of my first Trial Payment Plan, its failure to acknowledge my successful completion of a second Trial Payment Plan, and its XX/XX/XXXX denial of substantially all home-retention options. On XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom approved me for a Standalone Loan Modification subject to a three-month Trial Payment Plan. The plan required payments of {$2800.00} for XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. I accepted the plan and made the first XXXX required payments, totaling {$5600.00}. XXXX XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX mortgage statements reflect those payments. I expressly stated : I want to emphasize that I am fully committed to completing the Trial Period Plan in good faith and maintaining the loan going forward. I did not state that I was rejecting mortgage assistance, abandoning the XXXX XXXX XXXX, or refusing to comply with its terms. Nevertheless, on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom issued a letter stating that the program was not completed because of Borrower Rejected Current Workout. That characterization was inaccurate or, at minimum, materially misleading. My XX/XX/XXXX letter asked Freedom to consider an affordable permanent structure and expressly reaffirmed my commitment to the loss-mitigation process. I timely made all three payments under the second plan, totaling {$8300.00}. Freedom accepted the payments and, after I completed the plan, issued a permanent loan-modification approval dated XX/XX/XXXX. The proposed permanent modification required an estimated total monthly payment of {$2700.00}, including {$1300.00} in principal and interest and {$1300.00} in escrow. Because the payment was not sustainable, I submitted a written request on XX/XX/XXXX asking Freedom to reevaluate me for the FHA Payment Supplement, Partial Claim, Combination Loan Modification and Partial Claim, principal deferment, escrow review, and all other available FHA home-retention options. Freedom acknowledged that the XX/XX/XXXX request was a facially complete loss-mitigation application and stated that it would review me for all possible workout options. Nevertheless, Freedom issued a XX/XX/XXXX denial stating, among other things : Your loan has exceeded the limit for defaulted trial plans ; and You have failed to remit payments in accordance with the forbearance or trial plan you were approved for. The denial does not identify which XXXX XXXX XXXX Freedom claims was defaulted. It does not identify any particular missed payment, due date, or amount. It also fails to distinguish the incomplete first Trial Payment Plan from the second Trial Payment Plan that I successfully completed. The statement that I failed to remit payments under an approved trial plan is false as applied to the second plan. I made all three required payments, Freedom accepted them, and Freedom issued a permanent modification approval after the plan was completed. Freedoms XXXX denial is therefore inconsistent with its own payment records and its XX/XX/XXXX permanent-modification approval. Across both XXXX XXXX XXXX, I paid Freedom a total of {$14000.00}. I have requested a complete accounting showing how each payment was received, held, applied, or credited. I have also requested an explanation of the suspense and unapplied funds reflected on the mortgage statements and how those funds were treated when Freedom calculated the proposed modified principal balance. Freedom has not provided a transaction-level accounting demonstrating that the full {$14000.00} was properly credited once and that no amount was omitted, duplicated, misapplied, or added to the modified balance without a corresponding credit. I submitted a timely formal appeal to Freedom Mortgage on XX/XX/XXXX. A complete copy of that appeal, together with supporting Exhibits XXXX through XXXX, is attached to this CFPB complaint. Resolution Requested I request that Freedom Mortgage be required to : Conduct an independent review of its XX/XX/XXXX denial ; Correct the XX/XX/XXXX Borrower Rejected Current Workout characterization to reflect that I requested affordable permanent terms and did not reject mortgage assistance ; Identify every Trial Payment Plan that Freedom counts as defaulted, including the date, payment, amount, internal disposition, and FHA servicing code associated with each alleged default ; Confirm in writing that I successfully completed the XX/XX/XXXX Trial Payment Plan by making all three required payments totaling {$8300.00} ; Correct any internal or FHA record identifying the successfully completed second Trial Payment Plan as failed, rejected, withdrawn, or otherwise unsuccessful ; Explain the specific FHA XXXX under which an earlier incomplete Trial Payment Plan allegedly bars reconsideration after Freedom approved and I successfully completed a subsequent plan ; Reevaluate me for the FHA XXXX XXXX, Standalone Partial Claim, Combination Loan Modification and Partial Claim, principal deferment, and all other available FHA home-retention options ; Provide the calculations used for each option, including the unpaid principal balance, XXXX XXXX, delinquency cure amount, targeted principal-and-interest payment, interest rate, resulting payment, and precise basis for approval or denial ; Provide a complete accounting of all XXXX Trial Payment Plan payments totaling {$14000.00}, including the date received, amount applied, payment period credited, amount placed in suspense, amount remaining unapplied, and treatment of those funds in the proposed modified balance ; Correct any payment-history, loss-mitigation, or trial-plan coding errors ; Refrain from advancing foreclosure activity while my timely appeal and this servicing dispute remain under review; and If Freedom maintains that no FHA home-retention option is available, provide a fully itemized XXXX amount and the XXXX reasonable repayment arrangement available. I remain willing to make a sustainable mortgage payment and retain the property. I am not seeking to avoid my mortgage obligation. I am requesting accurate servicing records, a complete accounting of my payments, and a fair evaluation under the applicable FHA loss-mitigation requirements. Cordially, XXXX XXXX XXXX
