narrative: This complaint concerns Netspend 's dispute investigation and final denial, which occurred after my earlier CFPB complaint was filed. This is NOT a duplicate complaint regarding the underlying transactions but a complaint regarding the company 's investigation and denial of my dispute. I am filing this complaint regarding Netspend 's handling of my dispute under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( XXXX ) and Regulation XXXX. I previously reported unauthorized transactions on my account immediately after discovering them. Netspend completed its investigation and denied my claim. However, this complaint is not about re-reporting the unauthorized transactions. It concerns the adequacy of Netspend 's investigation and its dispute resolution process. The denial letter states only that there was : No pattern indicating fraud No evidence of account compromise No evidence of device compromise These are conclusory statements that do not explain what evidence was reviewed, how Netspend reached these conclusions, or why it determined the transactions were authorized. The denial provides no meaningful explanation of the investigation that was performed. A statement that there was " no evidence of device compromise '' does not establish that I authorized the transactions. Unauthorized electronic fund transfers can occur through a lost or stolen payment card or other unauthorized use without compromising the customer 's personal device. I requested that Netspend properly investigate my dispute. Instead, I received a denial that contains conclusions without supporting facts. I am requesting that Netspend provide all records relied upon in denying my claim, including investigation notes, transaction authentication records, login history, IP address information, device identifiers, merchant verification records, and any other documents used during its investigation. If Netspend can not produce evidence demonstrating that I authorized these transactions, I request that the company reopen the investigation, conduct a reasonable investigation consistent with Regulation XXXX, and reimburse the unauthorized transactions if appropriate. I respectfully ask the CFPB to review whether Netspend complied with its obligations under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation XXXX in investigating and denying my dispute.

narrative: I am filing a formal consumer complaint against Wells Fargo regarding their institutional failure to provide reasonable consumer hardship assistance programs for students, as well as structural policies that place unfair burdens on vulnerable consumers. On Friday, XX/XX/year>, I proactively contacted Wells Fargo credit card customer service to report a temporary financial transition. I transparently informed the representative that I am returning to higher education as a full-time student and currently have an immediate personal income of {$0.00}. I explained that I have a pending state unemployment claim, but because it has not yet been processed or approved, my future income remains unconfirmed. I asked if Wells Fargo offered any student hardship programs, short-term forbearance options, or temporary interest freezes to help keep my account stable while my financial situation transitions. The customer service representative was polite and empathetic, but she explained that from her standpoint, company policy provided absolutely no options or programs to pause payments or freeze interest under these circumstances. I attempted to negotiate, asking for hypothetical scenarios of what programs might open up if my unemployment is eventually approved at an estimated survival rate of {$800.00} a month. The representative was unable to provide any specific hypothetical solutions or concrete future options, noting only that I would have to call back after approval, but that payments are still currently required by the system. While the agent was respectful and noted that she felt bad about the situational constraints, she ultimately stated that she was bound by rigid company policy. During our conversation regarding my inability to pay with a {$0.00} income, she inquired if I had family members who could step in to assist with the monthly payments. While I understand she was likely following a standard internal script to find a solution, a corporate policy that prompts agents to suggest leveraging a consumer 's personal relationships to satisfy a credit card debt during a documented financial crisis is inappropriate and places immense psychological pressure on the consumer. Forcing a full-time student with a verified {$0.00} income to choose between managing basic survival needs or facing immediate delinquency due to a lack of corporate relief options is a severe systemic failure. I am requesting an executive review of this account 's constraints, a temporary freeze on late fees and compounding interest during this academic transition, and a formal evaluation of Wells Fargo 's hardship forbearance accessibility for students in financial transitions.

I am filing this complaint against I.C. System, Inc. regarding a collection account they are furnishing to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies on behalf of XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) in the approximate amount of {$470.00}. As a result, I was deprived of the opportunity to meaningfully evaluate or challenge the account before it negatively affected my credit profile. Because I dispute the account, I request that I.C. System produce competent evidence demonstrating both the validity of the alleged debt and the accuracy of every item of information it furnished to the consumer reporting agencies. Specifically, I request the following : The complete account history from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The original service agreement or other documentation establishing my legal responsibility for the account. The service address associated with the account. Every monthly billing statement. The final billing statement. A complete payment ledger. A detailed itemization explaining how the alleged balance of {$470.00} was calculated. Documentation showing the date the account was referred or assigned to I.C. System. Documentation establishing I.C. Systems authority to collect on behalf of XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. The date any validation notice was allegedly mailed. The address to which that notice was allegedly mailed. Documentation supporting every item of information reported to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I further request that I.C. System explain the procedures it used to determine that the information it furnished to the consumer reporting agencies was complete, accurate, and supported by competent documentation. As a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies, I.C. System has obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) to furnish information with accuracy and integrity. Information that can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation should not remain on a consumers credit report. Likewise, as a debt collector, I.C. System is expected to comply with the applicable requirements of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) concerning the collection of consumer debts and communications with consumers. If I.C. System contends that it complied with those obligations, I request that it produce the documentation supporting that position. If I.C. System can not produce competent documentation establishing : that I am legally responsible for the alleged debt, that the balance reported is accurate, that the account was properly reported, that it possessed authority to collect the account, and that its reporting complies with applicable federal law, then I request that this collection account be permanently deleted from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Merely stating that the account has been verified is insufficient. I request documentary evidence supporting the verification. I also request that the CFPB require I.C. System to conduct a reasonable investigation and provide copies of every document upon which it relies. Should I.C. System be unable to substantiate the account with competent documentary evidence, continued reporting would be inaccurate and misleading and should cease immediately. Accordingly, I respectfully request the following relief : Conduct a complete investigation into this disputed account. Require I.C. System to produce all documentation supporting the debt. Require I.C. System to explain the basis for furnishing the account to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies. Delete the account from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX if it can not be fully substantiated. Correct any inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading information. Confirm the results of the investigation in writing. I appreciate the CFPBs assistance in ensuring compliance with federal consumer protection laws and maintaining the accuracy of consumer credit reporting

Subject : CFPB Complaint Aargon Agency , Inc . Formal Dispute and Demand for Deletion of Unverified Collection Account I am filing this complaint against Aargon Agency , Inc. concerning its collection and credit reporting of an alleged XXXX XXXX account in the amount of {$180.00}. I dispute this alleged debt in its entirety. Pursuant to my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., I request a complete investigation and immediate correction of any inaccurate or unverifiable information. I demand that Aargon Agency , Inc. produce competent documentary evidence establishing that I am legally responsible for this alleged debt, including : * A copy of the original agreement or other evidence showing I am legally obligated for this account. * A complete itemized accounting showing how the alleged balance of {$180.00} was calculated. * Documentation establishing Aargon Agency, Inc.s authority to collect this account on behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXX through a lawful assignment. * Records identifying the date of default and the complete account history. * Copies of all documents relied upon when furnishing this account to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e, a debt collector may not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation in connection with the collection of a debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692f, a debt collector may not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect a debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, furnishers of information have a duty to investigate disputes and correct or delete information that can not be verified. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information reported. If Aargon Agency , Inc. can not provide competent evidence establishing my legal responsibility for this account, it must : * Immediately cease all collection activity. * Permanently delete this collection account from XXXX XXXX XXXX, and any other consumer reporting agency. * Notify each consumer reporting agency that the account has been deleted. * Provide written confirmation that the account has been permanently removed. Verification through automated systems such as e-OSCAR, internal database records, account summaries, or unsupported electronic records alone is insufficient to establish the legal validity of a disputed debt. A reasonable investigation requires review of competent documentary evidence. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate Aargon Agency , Inc.s compliance with the FDCPA and FCRA and require the company to correct or delete any information that can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation. If Aargon Agency , Inc. can not verify this alleged debt with competent evidence, I request the immediate and permanent deletion of this account from all consumer reporting agencies and the termination of all collection activity. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, NC XXXX

Had I received clear notice of the changes, I would have taken simple steps to avoid the fee, such as maintaining the required balance or switching to a more appropriate account type. Instead, I was charged without realizing that the previous practice was no longer available. I believe XXXX XXXX handling of this matter is unfair because : * I did not receive clear and timely notice regarding any changes affecting my account or the fee waiver policy. * Wells Fargo had previously granted courtesy fee waivers under similar circumstances, creating a reasonable expectation that a one-time adjustment would still be available. * I contacted the bank promptly after discovering the charge. * Despite my long-standing relationship with the bank and prior history, Wells Fargo refused to provide any goodwill adjustment or meaningful explanation. I am not requesting special treatment or an ongoing exemption from account fees. I am simply requesting a one-time goodwill refund because I reasonably relied on XXXX XXXXs long-standing practice of granting courtesy fee waivers under similar circumstances. Had I been properly informed of the changes beforehand, I would have avoided the fee entirely. I respectfully request that Wells Fargo : 1. Provide a one-time goodwill refund of the XXXX XXXX monthly service fee. 2. Review my account history, including previous courtesy fee waivers. 3. Explain when the account requirements or fee waiver practices changed. 4. Provide documentation showing how and when I was notified of those changes. 5. I asked if I could speak to a supervisor and after holding for about a half hour was told it could be hours before I could speak to a supervisor. I have been the victim of a complex scam once before that was much like this. I am very concerned that US Bank does not need to provide any verification of their identity and, if that text was legitimate, that it was, in fact, legitimate, and any ability on my part to verify that I am, in fact, speaking with US Bank. The most concerning part of this is that I was told that the transaction was declined by text, verified on phone, and told that neither could be validated. If US Bank is going to send texts about transactions, the information they provide should be correct, should lead to legitimate phone numbers, and should result in easily identifiable individuals and chain of command to ensure that I am not the victim of fraud, as much as they require much more of my personal information to ensure they are not the victim of fraud.

narrative: I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate the credit reporting practices of U.S. Bank Home Mortgage regarding my FHA mortgage. I entered a COVID-19 Recovery Standalone Partial Claim in XXXX and successfully completed all required trial payments. In its written response dated XX/XX/XXXX, U.S. Bank acknowledged that an oversight in its new loss mitigation system prevented completion of my approved Partial Claim. The bank also acknowledged that it sent documents containing incorrect dates and that, because of its own internal servicing error, the loss mitigation process had to be restarted. Despite admitting these servicing errors, U.S. Bank has refused to correct the negative credit reporting associated with my mortgage. My concern extends beyond the current reporting of late payments in XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. I believe the credit reporting reflects the same underlying delinquency twice because the original loss mitigation process failed due to U.S. Banks admitted servicing errors. My credit history reflects late payments during the original XXXX loss mitigation process. After U.S. Bank acknowledged that the approved Partial Claim could not be completed because of its own internal oversight and restarted the process, the account was again reported as seriously delinquent in XXXX. From my perspective, the account appears to have been returned to a delinquent status for the same underlying payment default that the original Partial Claim was intended to resolve. Had U.S. Bank completed the originally approved Partial Claim as intended, the second review would not have been necessary. Instead, the banks admitted servicing error resulted in the loss mitigation process being restarted, and my credit history now appears to reflect negative reporting associated with both the original process and the restarted process. I respectfully request that U.S. Bank explain : Whether the late payments reported in XXXX relate to the same underlying payment default that resulted in the XXXX Partial Claim approval. How it determined that additional delinquency reporting was appropriate after acknowledging that the original loss mitigation process failed because of its own servicing error. Why did the negative information continue to be furnished after the bank admitted that the completion of the Partial Claim was delayed due to an internal oversight rather than any failure on my part to make the required trial payments. Additionally, U.S. Banks letter states that I successfully completed all required trial payments for the newly approved Standalone Partial Claim and that the account was pending final documentation. However, my XXXX credit report simultaneously reported the account as 60 days past due and approximately {$4400.00} past due. I request a complete explanation of how those reported delinquencies were calculated while my account was proceeding through a second loss mitigation process necessitated by the banks own admitted servicing error. I respectfully request that U.S. Bank provide : 1. A complete payment history and servicing ledger. 2. A complete loss mitigation history for my account. XXXX. Documentation supporting every delinquency reported to XXXX XXXX, and XXXX from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. 4. An explanation of whether the 2025 and 2026 derogatory reporting relates to the same underlying delinquency. 5. A correction of any credit reporting that is inaccurate, duplicative, or otherwise inconsistent with the banks admitted servicing errors and the history of my approved Partial Claims. Because U.S. Bank has acknowledged that its own servicing mistakes disrupted my loss mitigation process, I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether the banks furnishing of negative credit information during this period was accurate and consistent with its obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and applicable mortgage servicing regulations. I also think we should include one additional sentence that I believe is particularly compelling : I should not suffer years of negative credit reporting because U.S. Banks own servicing errors prevented the timely completion of a loss mitigation program for which I had already been approved and whose required trial payments I successfully completed. That statement ties together the fairness concern without overstating the facts, and it highlights that the prolonged negative reporting followed from a servicing process the bank itself admits it mishandled.

narrative: I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate U.S. Bank National Association 's mortgage servicing practices, escrow administration, and the accuracy of representations made concerning my mortgage loan. I am currently involved in pending litigation concerning this mortgage loan. During my investigation, I have identified significant questions regarding U.S. Bank 's servicing records, escrow administration, communications with third parties, and the factual basis for representations made concerning my loan. My homeowner 's insurance company has represented through billing statements and its online customer portal that my homeowner 's insurance premiums are paid through an escrow account by my mortgage company and has identified U.S. Bank in connection with my homeowner 's insurance policy. However, I have personally made homeowner 's insurance premium payments, and I have repeatedly questioned the accuracy of those representations. I have submitted written requests to my insurance company seeking documentation identifying when U.S. Bank was associated with my policy, who requested that association, and what records support those representations. Because U.S. Bank is the mortgage servicer communicating information to third parties concerning my loan, I am requesting that CFPB require U.S. Bank to explain the factual basis for those communications and produce the business records supporting them. This complaint is not a request for CFPB to resolve the legal issues pending before the court. Rather, I request that CFPB require transparency regarding U.S. Bank 's servicing records, escrow records, and communications so that I may determine whether the information maintained concerning my mortgage loan is complete and accurate. Given the pending litigation, complete disclosure of the servicing records is important to ensure the accuracy of information maintained about my loan and to resolve inconsistencies regarding escrow administration and mortgage-related communications. Requested Response Please require U.S. Bank to answer each of the following in writing and identify the business records supporting each answer. State the legal and factual basis upon which U.S. Bank currently services my mortgage loan. Identify every agreement, transfer record, servicing record, boarding record, or other business record upon which U.S. Bank relies in servicing my loan. State the date U.S. Bank first began servicing my loan and identify the records supporting that date. Produce the complete servicing transfer history identifying each transferor, transferee, transfer date, and the business records documenting each transfer. State whether U.S. Bank has ever maintained an escrow account for homeowner 's insurance relating to my loan. If an escrow account existed, identify : when it was established ; every deposit ; every disbursement ; every insurance premium allegedly paid ; and the present status of the account. Produce the complete escrow accounting from the date U.S. Bank began servicing my loan through the present. Identify every homeowner 's insurance premium allegedly paid by U.S. Bank, including : payment date ; amount ; recipient ; payment method ; and supporting accounting records. Identify every communication between U.S. Bank and my homeowner 's insurance carrier regarding : homeowner 's insurance ; escrow ; mortgagee designation ; loss payee designation ; premium billing ; policy changes ; insurance claims. Produce every document transmitted by U.S. Bank to my homeowner 's insurance carrier identifying U.S. Bank as mortgagee, servicer, escrow administrator, or additional interest. Identify every document relied upon before representing to third parties that U.S. Bank was entitled to administer homeowner 's insurance matters relating to my loan. Identify every database, servicing platform, vendor, investor system, or third-party source from which U.S. Bank obtained information concerning my loan. State whether U.S. Bank has reviewed the accuracy of the information communicated to my homeowner 's insurance carrier after receiving notice that I dispute the servicing records. Identify every correction, if any, made after receiving notice of my dispute. State whether U.S. Bank possesses any additional servicing records, escrow records, communications, or documents concerning my loan that have not previously been disclosed to me. If any requested records do not exist, state that fact expressly and identify the reason those records are unavailable. Preserve all paper records, electronic records, emails, servicing notes, call recordings, audit logs, payment histories, escrow records, imaging systems, correspondence, and electronically stored information relating to my loan while this complaint and the related litigation remain pending. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that CFPB require U.S. Bank to provide complete, accurate, and documented responses supported by its business records, correct any inaccurate servicing information maintained concerning my loan, and preserve all records relating to my mortgage servicing, escrow administration, homeowner 's insurance communications, and payment history. I further request that U.S. Bank identify the source of every material factual assertion made in its response so that the information provided can be evaluated for completeness and accuracy. I certify that this complaint is submitted in good faith to obtain transparency regarding the servicing of my mortgage loan and the accuracy of the information maintained by U.S. Bank and communicate

narrative: Company 's name : Freedom Mortgage I enrolled in the companys biweekly mortgage payment program because the app represented it as a biweekly payment option. A reasonable consumer would understand this to mean that mortgage payments are transmitted to and applied by the mortgage servicer every two weeks. After contacting customer service, I was informed that the company does not actually send payments every two weeks. Instead, it withdraws funds from my bank account every two weeks, holds those funds, and sends a single monthly payment to the mortgage servicer on the normal due date. This material limitation was not clearly disclosed during enrollment. Had I known the payments were not actually being applied every two weeks, I would not have enrolled in the service because one of my primary goals was to reduce interest by lowering my principal balance sooner. I believe the apps presentation of this feature is misleading and request that the company clearly disclose how the program actually works and provide any appropriate remedy if consumers were misled.
